translation:
HRCT of the Lungs

The examination was performed in a survey phase with continuous slices of 1.25 and 2.5 mm thickness during inspiration and expiration.

Referral data: COPD, pulmonary fibrosis, assessment of changes.

Examination Description:

Features of lung hyperinflation. The average lung density during the inspiratory phase ranges from approximately minus 873 to minus 930 Hounsfield units. In segment VI of the right lung, there is a multi-lobular area measuring 30x15mm of panlobular emphysema with a density of about minus 950 Hounsfield units. No emphysematous bullae, pan- and centrilobular emphysema, or paraseptal emphysema are observed. There are single fibrous streaks and bands of plate-like atelectasis in segments V, VIII, IX, and X of the right lung and segments V, VIII, and X of the left lung. No other changes in the lungs are noted.

Segmental mild, cylindrical bronchiectasis in segment X of the lungs. No other changes in the trachea or bronchial tree are visualized.

Pleural cavities are free of fluid.

No enlarged lymph nodes are observed in the mediastinum, pulmonary hila, or axillary regions.

The heart is not enlarged.

The major mediastinal vessels are not dilated.

The visualized bony structures show no signs of malignant structural remodeling.

Moderately pronounced degenerative changes in the thoracic spine, with the presence of marginal vertebral body spurs, single osteophytes, and small defects near the endplates of the lower thoracic vertebrae.

The partially visualized upper abdominal organs show no signs of pathology.

Conclusions:

Features of lung hyperinflation. In segment VI of the right lung, a multi-lobular area of panlobular emphysema. Single fibrous bands in both lungs.

translation:
HRCT of the lungs was performed with 0.6 and 1.2 mm slices, during inspiration and expiration, without intravenous contrast.

Referral information: Suspected HP. Follow-up.

Examination description:

A comparative assessment was made with the previous examination.

In the lower lobes of both lungs, there are extensive ground-glass opacities increasing caudally - slight progression noted.

Reticular thickening of the interlobular septa in the lower lobes is similar to the previous examination.

Trace microcystic "honeycombing" changes in the right posterior costophrenic recess - stable.

At the posterior surface of the lower lobes, there are band-like and reticular consolidations showing mild progression compared to the previous examination.

In the posterior costophrenic recesses, confluent consolidations appear similar to the previous examination.

Mosaic attenuation in the lower lobes of both lungs is comparable to the previous examination.

The nodular changes in both lungs remain stable.

Slight progression of ground-glass opacities in the upper lobe of the left lung below the pulmonary hilum.

Reticular interstitial densities and subtle ground-glass areas are comparable to the previous examination, also present at the base of the right middle lobe.

The heart is not enlarged.

Mediastinal lymph nodes are not significantly enlarged.

Lymph nodes in groups IV and VII contain fatty sinuses.

The included parts of the epigastrium show no pathology.

Bony structures show no pathological remodeling.

Minor degenerative changes in the thoracic spine.

Conclusions:

Compared to the previous examination: minimal progression of ground-glass opacities mainly in the lower lobes of both lungs, minimal progression of irregular consolidated densities at the posterior surface of the lower lobes, and mosaic attenuation of the lungs.

The number and size of nodular, reticular interstitial densities remain stable compared to the previous examination.

Otherwise, as described.

The examination was performed sequentially with slice thicknesses of 2.5 and 0.6 mm in the survey phase. Due to motion artifacts, the scan was repeated.

Clinical Data: Status post facial and head trauma. Under the influence of alcohol.

Examination Description:

No evidence of acute intracranial hemorrhage, edema, or expansive lesions.

Deepening of the cerebral sulci at the convexity and the upper cerebellar fissures.

The ventricular system is not enlarged, not displaced, and symmetrical.

Midline structures are not displaced.

The density of the brain's white and gray matter is normal.

Segmental, slight thickening of the mucosa in the ethmoid cells. Otherwise, the paranasal sinuses and the petrous parts of the temporal bones included in the study are normally aerated.

Fracture of the upper-anterior part of the nasal septum - old? Atrophy of the left eyeball.

Otherwise, the skull bones show no pathological structural remodeling or revealed post-traumatic changes.

Normal CT appearance of the cranio-cervical junction.

Conclusions:

Apart from atrophic deepening of the cerebral sulci at the convexity and the upper cerebellar fissures, no pathological changes in the brain were visualized. Otherwise, as described.

translation:
Virtual Colonoscopy

The examination was performed with a 1.2 mm slice thickness after insufflation of air into the colon. Scanning in the prone position was done in the survey phase, and scanning in the supine position was performed after intravenous administration of 90 ml of Omnipaque 350 contrast agent without early complications. Prior to the examination, 1 ampoule of Buscolysin was administered intramuscularly.

Clinical Data: Exclusion of organic changes. Numerous adhesions following gynecological surgery made colonoscopy examination impossible.

Examination Description:

A hiatal hernia measuring up to 52x37x51 mm, with the cardia and fundus of the stomach located subdiaphragmatically. Other parts of the chest included in the examination show no changes.

A small amount of residual fluid in the cecum, ascending colon, and segmentally in the transverse colon.

Diagnostic distension of all segments of the colon was achieved.

Three additional benign bends in the transverse colon.

The ileocecal valve is incompetent, with some of the insufflated air passing into the small intestine, revealing an unchanged terminal ileum.

No pathological wall thickening or polyps over 5 mm were observed in the colon. The appendix is unchanged. Pericolic fat tissue is unchanged. Few diverticula in the sigmoid and descending colon, up to 6 mm in size.

The liver, in a single-phase study (in the survey and venous phases), is homogeneous, not enlarged, with a 5 mm cyst in segment 2.

The gallbladder, bile ducts, and biliary system are unchanged.

Hepatic veins are not dilated.

The spleen is homogeneous without heterogeneous changes. A small accessory spleen, about 6 mm in size, is present near the spleen.

The pancreas shows no changes in the single-phase study (in the survey and venous phases).

Adrenal glands have a normal appearance.

The kidneys are in normal position and size, without focal changes, stasis, or stones. They typically enhance post-contrast. No enlarged lymph nodes are observed along the major vessels.

No intraperitoneal implants are visible. Status post-removal of the reproductive organ.

Increased density of mesenteric fat tissue - features of lipodystrophy.

The bladder is moderately filled with urine, with smooth walls.

The aorta, common and external iliac arteries are patent and not dilated.

The skeletal system shows no malignant structural remodeling.

Degenerative changes in the vertebral bodies of the lower thoracic spine.

Conclusions:

No significant pathological changes in the colon were observed. Liver cyst. Status post-removal of the reproductive organ.

Increased density of mesenteric fat tissue - features of lipodystrophy. Hiatal hernia with the cardia and fundus of the stomach located subdiaphragmatically.

translation:
CT of the chest.

The examination was performed with slice thicknesses of 5, 2.5, and 1.25 mm, before and after intravenous administration of 70 ml of Omnipaque 350 contrast agent, without early complications.

Referral data: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia. Rheumatoid arthritis. Multiple sclerosis. The radiologist describes small nodular changes in the right lung at the level of the third rib and in the apex of the left lung on X-ray.

Examination description:

Typical perifissural nodules at the outline of the right horizontal fissure, up to 4 mm in size—non-suspicious changes, corresponding to intrapulmonary lymph nodes. Linear interstitial bands—scar-like in the right upper lobe segment III. The appearance of these changes is similar to the previous examination.

In the left lower lobe segment VIII, near the outline of the oblique fissure, there is an area of subsegmental scar-related atelectasis, slightly more consolidated than in the previous examination, currently with a smaller air bronchogram than before. Otherwise, the lungs show no revealing changes and have normal architecture.

The tracheobronchial tree is unchanged.

Pleural cavities are free.

Pleural layers are not thickened.

No heterogeneous structures or enlarged lymph nodes are observed in the mediastinum or pulmonary hila.

Major mediastinal vessels are not dilated.

The abdominal organs included in the examination show no changes.

The skeletal system shows no malignant remodeling. Degenerative changes with multilevel degeneration of the intervertebral discs in the thoracic spine. A fracture of the upper endplate of the L1 vertebral body with a reduction in its height in the middle part and an intravertebral hernia, as in the previous examination.

Conclusions: In the left lower lobe segment VIII, an area of scar-related atelectasis is slightly more consolidated than in the previous examination, currently with a smaller air bronchogram than before. Otherwise, the appearance of the chest organs shows no significant changes, stable compared to the previous examination.

translation:
CT of the Paranasal Sinuses 02/04/2022

The examination was performed with slices of 1.2/0.6 mm thickness, using both soft tissue and bone algorithms in the survey phase, with secondary multiplanar reconstruction.

Examination Description:

The paranasal sinuses are normally developed. The ethmoid roof is of Kerost type III.

The frontal and sphenoid sinuses are normally aerated on both sides, showing no abnormalities. Supraorbital ethmoid cells are present.

The ethmoid air cells are mostly aerated, without pathological features, except for segmental thickening of the mucous membrane.

The right maxillary sinus is completely non-aerated, filled with masses of heterogeneous fluid-tissue density (ranging from 8 to a maximum of 74 Hounsfield units) with an expansile growth pattern. The highest density of the mass is in the medial part of the alveolar recess. These masses protrude through the enlarged opening and defects in the medial wall of the sinus into the nasal cavity. The continuity of the medial bony wall of the sinus is difficult to trace. The sinus opening to the middle nasal meatus is widened to approximately 18mm (anterior-posterior). The remaining bony walls of the sinus are moderately expanded.

Tissue masses measuring approximately 38x10x43mm (cranio-caudal x superior-inferior x anterior-posterior) in the right nasal cavity completely fill the middle nasal meatus, causing displacement and partial atrophy/compression or destruction? of the middle turbinate. They almost completely occupy the superior nasal meatus and the medial part of the inferior nasal meatus. They also protrude into several ethmoid cells on the right in the middle part.

Otherwise, the bony elements of the walls of the paranasal sinuses show no signs of pathological remodeling.

The left maxillary sinus contains several polypoid, smooth-contoured structures, with a density of about 25 Hounsfield units and a diameter up to 6mm near the sinus opening and up to 12mm in the alveolar recess.

The openings of the frontal and sphenoid sinuses and the left ostiomeatal complex are patent. The remaining sinus openings and the right ostiomeatal complex are occupied by tissue-fluid masses.

Pneumatization of the left nasal turbinate with partial involvement of the cavity by a mucosal thickening approximately 5mm in diameter. Otherwise, the nasal turbinates on the left side appear normal.

The nasal passages on the left side maintain patency.

The nasal septum is straight.

Teeth 18 and 28 are unerupted.

In the greater wing of the sphenoid bone on the left side, there is sclerotic remodeling of the bone structure consistent with fibrous dysplasia, measuring approximately 21.5x11x14mm.

Conclusions: Pathological tissue-fluid masses in the right maxillary sinus and nasal cavity of indeterminate character. Differential diagnosis includes antrochoanal polyp, inverted papilloma, nerve sheath tumor, or mixed tumor.

translation:
HRCT of the Lungs

The examination was performed during inspiration and expiration with continuous slices of 1.2 and 2.5 mm thickness, in the survey phase.

Clinical Data: Bronchial asthma. History of sarcoidosis. Post-respiratory tract infection. Evaluation of lung tissue.

Examination Description:

In the lower lobes, predominantly basilar and subpleural, there is reticular thickening of the stroma with slight traction bronchiectasis/bronchiolectasis, more pronounced on the right side. Against this background, calcified micronodules are present in segment 10 of the right lung. Scattered small nodular and nodular consolidations up to 4 mm are observed in both lungs, with the largest nodule in segment 2 of the right lung. The remaining micronodules are mainly in the peripheral parts of the lungs. There is a trace of linear and micronodular interstitial changes in the anterior, subpleural parts of the upper lobes. Micronodules are noted along the outline of the interlobar fissures, mainly the left oblique fissure.

A few calcified bronchopulmonary lymph nodes are present in the lower lobe of the right lung.

No areas of air trapping are observed in the expiratory phase of the examination. Otherwise, the lungs show no changes. The tracheobronchial tree is patent. No heterogeneous structures or enlarged lymph nodes are observed in the mediastinum.

The major mediastinal vessels are not dilated. The heart is not enlarged.

The pleural layers are not thickened. No fluid is detected in the pleural cavities or pericardial sac.

The liver density in the survey phase is within normal limits. Status post-cholecystectomy. The skeletal system shows no malignant structural remodeling. There are moderately pronounced degenerative changes in the thoracic vertebral bodies. Degenerative changes are also noted in the right acromioclavicular joint, with a small bone island in the proximal end of the right humerus and in the right acetabulum.

Conclusions:

Nonspecific interstitial consolidations in the basilar parts of the lower lobes and less pronounced subpleurally in the anterior parts of the upper lobes of the lungs. Otherwise, as described.

translation:
CT of the Chest

The examination was performed with slice thicknesses of 2.5 and 1 mm before and after intravenous administration (without early complications) of 60 ml of Omnipaque 350 contrast agent.

Clinical Data: Chest CT with contrast. Hemoptysis for 2 weeks. D-dimers within normal range.

Examination Description:

In the lower lobe of the right lung, mainly in segment 7 and partially in adjacent areas of segments 8, 9, and 10, there is a cobblestone pattern consolidation measuring approximately 5 x 6 cm, correlating with clinical data indicative of alveolar hemorrhage in the subacute phase.

Within this area, near the outline of the left lower pulmonary vein, there is a solid nodular consolidation measuring approximately 15 x 8 mm.

In both lungs, numerous, uncountable small nodular and nodular consolidations with random distribution, ranging in size from 1.5 to 11 mm, with varied morphology: solid, partially solid, and a few cavitating nodules. The largest partially solid nodule is in segment 10 of the right lung. There are multiple cylindrical bronchiectases in the lungs, most pronounced in segments 10, 9, and 3, in the lingula, and in segment 5 of the right lung. There is marked reticular thickening of the stroma along the vascular-bronchial bundles in the areas of the most altered bronchiectatic bronchial tree.

There is a sliding hiatal hernia with the cardia and fundus of the stomach located in the thoracic cavity, with the hernia opening measuring up to 23 mm.

No heterogeneous structures or enlarged lymph nodes are visible in the mediastinum or pulmonary hila. The largest lymph nodes measure up to 8 mm in groups 12L and 10R. The heart is not enlarged. There is fluid in the pericardial recesses. Calcification of the coronary artery walls and possible stents are noted.

The pleural plaques are not thickened. No fluid is detected in the pleural cavities or pericardial sac.

The major mediastinal vessels are not dilated and are patent.

The abdominal organs included in the study show no changes.

The skeletal system shows no malignant structural remodeling.

There is increased kyphosis, signs of osteopenia, and productive changes in the thoracic spine. A hemangioma is present in the body of the Th5 vertebra.

Conclusions: In the lower lobe of the right lung, there is an area of subacute alveolar hemorrhage.

In both lungs, there are small nodular and nodular consolidations, some with cavitations - suspicion of a neoplastic process. Further pulmonary diagnostics are necessary.

translation:
CT of the cervical spine.

The examination was performed spirally with 1.2 mm slices using soft tissue and bone algorithms, with multiplanar and volumetric reconstructions.

Examination Description:

Loss of cervical lordosis.

Normal appearance of the cranio-cervical junction and proper alignment of the odontoid process relative to the anterior arch of C1.

The heights of the cervical vertebral bodies, their alignment with each other, and with T1 are normal.

Intra-body herniation with a segmentally concave outline of the superior endplate of the T1 vertebral body.

Degenerative changes in the facet joints at C2/C3 and C3/C4 on the right side and C2/C3 on the left side.

Deforming degenerative changes in the uncovertebral joints at the levels of C5/C6 and C6/C7 bilaterally, and to a lesser extent at C4/C5.

Osteophytosis of the anterolateral edges of the vertebral bodies from C2 to C7 and the posterior edges of the vertebral bodies from C4 to C7, with their protrusion into the spinal canal, modeling the dural sac and causing secondary narrowing of the sagittal dimension of the spinal canal.

No malignant bone restructuring is observed.

At levels C3 to C7, there is a reduction in the height of the intervertebral discs (especially at C5/C6 and C6/C7) and posterior protrusions of the intervertebral discs. At these levels, secondary bone proliferative changes predominate.

Conclusions:

Flattening of the lordosis and features of spondyloarthrosis of the cervical spine, most pronounced at the levels of C5/C6 and C6/C7.

translation:
CT of the Abdomen and Pelvis

The examination was performed with a slice thickness of 1.2 mm in the survey phase.

Clinical Data: Epigastric pain. Elevated amylase. Suspected pancreatitis. Epigastric region not assessable by ultrasound. Status post-cholecystectomy.

Examination Description:

The value of the study is limited by the absence of intravenous contrast administration.

In the included basal parts of the lungs, no significant pathological changes were observed, only age-related changes. Prominent esophageal bulb.

In segment 7 of the liver, a 10mm hypodense focal lesion is noted. Dilation of the intrahepatic bile ducts and the common bile duct is dilated between 13 and 17mm. A peripapillary diverticulum of the duodenum measuring approximately 30mm.

Otherwise, the liver, spleen, and kidneys appear normal on the survey scan.

Gallbladder not visible - removed.

The pancreas shows slightly blurred lobular architecture, with no other changes revealed in the survey phase. Peripancreatic fat tissue is unchanged.

In the adrenal glands, 11mm hypodense nodules with negative densities (benign in nature).

Ureters are not dilated, no stones.

Bladder poorly filled with urine, no changes revealed.

Small calcifications in the uterus.

Large abdominal and pelvic vessels are not dilated. No enlarged lymph nodes along the major vessels.

Ischiorectal fossae are clear.

Diverticulosis of the sigmoid colon.

Skeletal system without malignant structural remodeling. Right-sided curvature and degenerative changes in the vertebral and joint structures of the lumbar spine (protruding into the canal) with multilevel intervertebral disc degeneration.

Conclusions: The value of the study is limited by the absence of intravenous contrast administration. The pancreas shows slightly blurred lobular architecture, with no other changes revealed in the survey phase, which does not exclude inflammation. Dilation of the bile ducts. Status post-cholecystectomy. Peripapillary diverticulum of the duodenum.

Otherwise, as described.

translation:
CT of the abdomen.

The examination was performed with 1.25 mm slices before and multiphase (pancreatic protocol) after intravenous administration of 80 ml of contrast agent Ultravist 370, without early complications.

Clinical data: Newly diagnosed diabetes. Post-inflammatory changes? in the pancreas. Cystic changes near the pylorus to be evaluated in CT.

Examination description:

First examination in our CT lab.

No pleural fluid detected above the diaphragm. The lower parts of the lungs included in the examination show no changes.

The liver measures 14.1 x 16.9 cm (CC x AP) in the midclavicular line, with normal density and no focal lesions.

Intrahepatic bile ducts are visible/prominent, without significant dilation. The common bile duct measures up to 8.5 mm in the pre-pancreatic segment, slightly wider, and is not visible in the pancreatic segment.

The gallbladder has a congested, non-thickened wall, with no visible stones on CT, and is not enlarged.

The tail of the pancreas is atrophic with an irregularly dilated pancreatic duct up to 3.5 mm, with small, sparse periductal calcifications. The body of the pancreas is not enlarged, with a fairly smoothly dilated pancreatic duct up to 7 mm and small calcifications in the parenchyma. The upper part of the pancreatic head is heterogeneous and slightly hypodense over an area of approximately 20 x 18 mm, with small parenchymal calcifications. The rest of the pancreatic head is not enlarged, with numerous parenchymal/periductal calcifications. In the pancreatic head, the dilated pancreatic duct up to 7.5 mm contains stones, the largest being up to 8 mm in the periampullary segment.

In the medial wall of the duodenal bulb and the initial segment of the descending part of the duodenum, there are closely located fluid spaces of pseudocystic nature (with wall enhancement) measuring up to 25 mm and 18 mm on transverse scans. They may be connected by a narrow stalk. They narrow the intestinal lumen. There is no fat tissue separation from the adjacent pancreatic head. In their vicinity (medially and below), in the hepatoduodenal ligament, subdiaphragmatically, near the left adrenal gland, there are numerous homogeneous lymph nodes with a short axis from 6 to 13 mm - the largest near the mesenteric vessel branches in the mid-abdomen and behind the portal vein.

The celiac trunk, superior mesenteric artery and branches, portal vein with tributaries are patent, without luminal narrowing/obstruction and without signs of infiltration.

Simple cyst of 29 mm in the left kidney. Two left renal arteries.

Otherwise, the CT image of the abdominal organs (adrenals, kidneys, spleen, gastrointestinal tract) shows no pathological changes.

The skeletal system shows no pathological structural remodeling.

Conclusions:

Chronic calcifying pancreatitis (possibly due to periduodenal inflammation).

However, due to the lack of history of previous episodes of pancreatitis and the presence of numerous lymph nodes, the coexistence of pancreatic cancer cannot be definitively excluded. Consultation at a referral center is recommended.

translation:
Examination Description:
The lower parts of the chest included in the study show no abnormalities. There is an additional interlobar fissure in the lower lobe of the right lung, partially separating segment 7 - a developmental variant.
The liver is of normal size and density, homogeneous. In the craniocaudal dimension in the right midclavicular line, it measures up to 13.3 cm. In segment 4, there is a small, subcapsular 7 mm wedge-shaped hyperdense lesion - likely a THAD/hemangioma or vascular shunt. Otherwise, the liver shows no focal lesions in all phases of the study.
The gallbladder is not enlarged, has thin walls, and no calculi are visible on CT.
The intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts are not dilated. The branches of the portal system and hepatic veins are patent. The perivascular spaces are prominently marked and widened.
The spleen is not enlarged and is homogeneous in the venous phase. In its vicinity, there are two small accessory spleens.
The pancreas shows no heterogeneous changes and is sausage-shaped.
The shape, size, and position of both adrenal glands are normal.
The kidneys are in normal position and size. In the middle calyx of the left kidney, there is a 2 mm punctate calculus. The kidneys enhance typically with contrast, without focal changes. The renal collecting systems and ureters are not dilated. The walls of the right renal pelvis and the upper segment of the right ureter are marked/swollen and slightly enhance with contrast - indicative of inflammatory changes or possibly a recent passage of a calculus.
The major abdominal vessels are patent.
No enlarged lymph nodes are seen along the major vessels.
Within the limits of the method's capability, the bowel loops and stomach show no abnormalities.
No free gas or fluid is detected in the peritoneal cavity.
The skeletal system shows no malignant structural remodeling.

Conclusions: Widened perivascular spaces. A small calculus in the middle calyx of the left kidney. Swollen and mildly contrast-enhancing walls of the right renal pelvis and upper segment of the right ureter - indicative of inflammatory changes or possibly a recent passage of a calculus. Otherwise, as described.

translation:
CT of the Brain.

The examination was performed in the survey phase with 1 mm and 3 mm slices using soft tissue and bone algorithms.

Examination Description:

No evidence of acute intracranial hemorrhage was observed. In the right occipital lobe, there is a small area of edema measuring 20 mm with a moderately hyperdense center, resembling an ischemic change with features of laminar necrosis and luxury perfusion. In the angiographic phase, it shows signs of hyperemia. Otherwise, the tissue density of the white and gray matter structures of the brain is normal. The supratentorial ventricular system is of normal size, symmetrical, and not displaced. The configuration of the basal cisterns is typical. The posterior fossa structures and the fourth ventricle are unchanged (beam hardening artifacts present). No pathological changes were observed in the bony structures of the skull. Calcification of the walls of the cavernous and clinoid segments of the ICA.

Conclusions: Completed, fresh ischemic focus in the right occipital lobe. ASPECTS.

Największe z obszarów objętych niedokrwieniem lokalizują się w obrębie prawego płata potylicznego wielkości 23 x 31 mm (z widocznym wzmocnieniem pokontrastowym wzdłuż zakrętów) oraz w obrębie prawego płata ciemieniowego o wym. 35 x 14 mm; zmianom tym towarzyszy zwężenie bruzd i rowków mózgowych. Mnogie, zlewne obszary tego typu widoczne również w wieńcu promienistym po prawej stronie. Najmniej liczne zmiany widoczne w obrębie zakrętów płata czołowego i wyspy. Obszary zmian malacyjnych z towarzyszącą gliozą widoczne w prawym płacie czołowym i lewym płacie skroniowym - przewlekłe zmiany niedokrwienne. Układ komorowy nadnamiotowy nieprzemieszczony, nieposzerzony, symetryczny. Wodociąg mózgu, komora IV bez zmian. Struktury tylnojamowe bez zmian. Umiarkowane poszerzenie bruzd mózgowia. Okrężne zgrubienia śluzówki sitowia. Innych zmian nie stwierdza się.

Wnioski: Mnogie ogniska dokonanego udaru niedokrwiennego prawej półkuli mózgu w zakresie unaczynienia R-MCA. Przewlekłe zmiany niedokrwienne w obrębie zakrętów prawego płata czołowego i lewego skroniowego.
translation:
MRI of the brain.

The examination was performed with the administration of 8.5 ml of Gadovist 1 MOL intravenously.

Examination description:

Within the right hemisphere of the brain, across all lobes, multiple foci are visible, showing diffusion restriction characteristics and elevated signals on FLAIR images. These changes correspond to multiple ischemic stroke foci within the vascular territory of the right middle cerebral artery (R-MCA). The largest ischemic areas are located in the right occipital lobe, measuring 23 x 31 mm (with visible post-contrast enhancement along the gyri), and in the right parietal lobe, measuring 35 x 14 mm; these changes are accompanied by narrowing of the sulci and grooves of the brain. Multiple confluent areas of this type are also visible in the right corona radiata. The least numerous changes are seen in the gyri of the frontal lobe and insula. Areas of malacic changes with accompanying gliosis are visible in the right frontal lobe and left temporal lobe, indicating chronic ischemic changes. The supratentorial ventricular system is not displaced, not enlarged, and symmetrical. The cerebral aqueduct and the fourth ventricle are unchanged. Posterior fossa structures are unchanged. Moderate widening of the cerebral sulci. Circumferential thickening of the ethmoid sinus mucosa. No other changes are noted.

Conclusions: Multiple foci of completed ischemic stroke in the right hemisphere of the brain within the R-MCA vascular territory. Chronic ischemic changes in the gyri of the right frontal lobe and left temporal lobe.

Prawa tętnica środkowa mózgu (MCA) w odcinku M1 jest niedrożna na długości 7 mm. Odcinki M2, M3 i M4 są drożne, ale nieznacznie węższe niż po stronie lewej. Obie tętnice tylne mózgu (PCA), przednie mózgu (ACA), lewa tętnica środkowa mózgu (MCA) w odcinkach 1 i 2 oraz ich główne odgałęzienia są drożne. Tętnica łącząca przednia jest niezmieniona, natomiast tętnice łączące tylne są niewidoczne - wariant rozwojowy. Tętniakowatego poszerzenia naczyń oraz malformacji tętniczo-żylnych nie stwierdza się. Zatoki opony twardej są drożne. Zmiany zwyrodnieniowe w trzonach kręgowych oraz stawach odcinka szyjnego kręgosłupa z obniżeniem wysokości przestrzeni międzykręgowych C4/C5/C6 na tle dyskopatii.

translation:
CT Angiography of the Neck and Cerebral Arteries

The examination was performed following the administration of a contrast agent, with a slice thickness of 1 mm.

Examination Description:

The aortic arch is patent and not dilated. The pulmonary trunk and the visualized segments of the pulmonary arteries are patent and not dilated. The brachiocephalic trunk, right and left subclavian arteries, as well as both common carotid arteries (CCA), are patent, with no significant stenosis or dilation of the lumen. The proximal segment of the right internal carotid artery (ICA) shows a double kink. Calcification of the walls is observed in the cavernous and clinoid segments of both ICAs. The left vertebral artery arises directly from the aortic arch, with no other abnormalities. The basilar artery is patent and not stenosed. The right middle cerebral artery (MCA) is occluded in the M1 segment over a length of 7 mm. The M2, M3, and M4 segments are patent but slightly narrower than on the left side. Both posterior cerebral arteries (PCA), anterior cerebral arteries (ACA), the left middle cerebral artery (MCA) in segments 1 and 2, and their main branches are patent. The anterior communicating artery is unchanged, while the posterior communicating arteries are not visible, which is a developmental variant. There is no evidence of aneurysmal dilation of vessels or arteriovenous malformations. The dural venous sinuses are patent. Degenerative changes are noted in the vertebral bodies and joints of the cervical spine, with reduced height of the intervertebral spaces at C4/C5/C6 due to discopathy.

Conclusions: The M1 segment of the right middle cerebral artery (MCA) is segmentally occluded over a length of 7 mm.

translation:
Abdominal Ultrasound Examination

Referral Information: Suspected right-sided renal colic, hematuria

The examination was performed using an Arietta 750 machine with a convex probe.

Examination Description:

The liver is of normal size and echogenicity, with no focal lesions visible. The intrahepatic bile ducts are not dilated. The hepatic veins and branches of the portal system are patent. The gallbladder is free of stones, with several polyps up to 4 mm in size, consistent with hyperplastic cholecystosis. The spleen is not enlarged and is homogeneous. The pancreas is visible in the head and body regions, with normal echogenicity and no focal lesions. The tail of the pancreas is not visible. The Wirsung duct is not dilated. The kidneys are in normal position and size, with no stones. The right kidney measures 128 x 41 mm, with dilated calyces ranging from 14 to 21 mm and a thinned parenchymal layer from 6 to 10 mm, with no visible stones. The upper end of the DJ stent is visible in the non-dilated renal pelvis. The sub-pelvic segment of the right ureter is not dilated. The left kidney measures 113 x 50 mm, with a normal appearance. The urinary bladder is poorly filled, smooth-walled, and not assessable. The prostate gland measures 30 x 26 x 42 x 38 mm. The major abdominal and pelvic vessels are not dilated. The periaortic region is unchanged.

Conclusions: DJ stent with the upper end in the right renal pelvis, the lower end of the stent is not visible. Thinning of the cortical layer of the right kidney and dilation of its calyces.

translation:

translation:
CT Scan of the Chest

The examination was performed with 2.5 mm slices and secondary reconstruction at 1.25 mm, before and after intravenous administration of 7 ml of Visipaque 320 contrast agent.

Referral data: Two-month-old female infant - right adrenal mass. Please evaluate the thoracic organs.

Examination description:

Lungs show no focal lesions. Pleural cavities are free of fluid. The trachea and major bronchi are of normal size, with no signs of bronchiectasis. No enlarged peritracheal lymph nodes are visible. Pulmonary hilar lymph nodes measure 4 x 8 mm on the right and 4 x 2 mm on the left. The thymus tissue structure is of homogeneous density, measuring 18 mm AP, 33 mm transverse, and 48 mm craniocaudal. The heart is not enlarged, and there is no fluid in the pericardial sac. The thyroid gland, within the visible range, is of homogeneous density. Partially visible abdominal organs: liver, segment VI, shows a focal lesion (not fully captured in the study), measuring 25 mm AP and 36 mm transverse. Before contrast administration, it is hypodense with calcifications present; after contrast, it enhances well, with a visible vessel connecting the lesion to the right branch of the portal vein. Adrenal glands are unremarkable bilaterally. Bone structures show no signs of malignant transformation. At the level of the chest, in the subcutaneous fat tissue, a few nodular changes up to 3 mm in diameter are visible. A 10 x 6 mm structure in the left axillary region may correspond to a lymph node.

Conclusions:

Lungs show no visible focal changes. The liver lesion in segment VI, with calcifications, enhances well after contrast administration. Hepatoblastoma is considered in the differential diagnosis, although other characteristics of the lesion cannot be excluded.

translation:
Abdominal Ultrasound Examination

The examination was performed using a Hitachi device on an urgent, emergency basis.

Examination Description:

In segment VI of the liver, there is a solid-cystic, heterogeneous focal lesion measuring 2.6 x 2.7 x 3.0 cm with central calcifications; the lesion has polycyclic contours, is subcapsular, and shows rich vascularization on color Doppler - the image is inconclusive. I suggest further diagnostic evaluation with an accelerated, scheduled MRI with contrast. Otherwise, the liver has normal echogenicity, homogeneous structure, no other focal lesions, and is not enlarged. The gallbladder is anechoic and contracted. Intrahepatic bile ducts are not dilated. The pancreas and the area of the major vessels are obscured by intestinal gases. The spleen is homogeneous and not enlarged. The kidneys are of normal size, without signs of stasis or focal changes, with normal parenchymal-sinus differentiation. The urinary bladder is well-filled with urine, thin-walled, and anechoic. The reproductive organs are age-appropriate. Examination with a linear probe shows non-dilated intestinal loops with non-thickened walls and visible peristalsis. No free fluid is observed in the peritoneal cavity. Documentation with measurements is in the RIS system.

Conclusions:

Focal liver lesion of indeterminate nature - I suggest further diagnostic evaluation with an accelerated, scheduled MRI with contrast.

translation:
Abdominal Ultrasound

The examination was performed using an Aloka machine on an urgent basis.

Examination Description:

The liver is enlarged, measuring 20x19.8 cm, with increased echogenicity consistent with fatty infiltration and a homogeneous structure, without focal lesions. The gallbladder contains concentrated bile, has thin walls, and no visible stones. The liver hilum is partially obscured by intestinal gas. The intrahepatic bile ducts, portal vessels, and hepatic veins are not dilated within the visible range. The kidneys are in their typical position, of normal size, with preserved corticomedullary differentiation, and show no signs of obstruction, stones, or focal lesions. The pancreas is not clearly visible. The spleen is homogeneous, not enlarged, with a bipolar dimension of 10.8 cm. The abdominal aorta is partially obscured by intestinal gas, visible in the mid-abdomen, and not dilated. The urinary bladder is well-filled with urine and has smooth, thin walls. The prostate is not enlarged. Free fluid in the peritoneal cavity is noted: up to 5 mm near the visceral surface of the liver, up to 11 mm near the lateral surface of the liver, below the rounded lower edge of the liver with separation up to 52x33 mm (APxSD), and near the bladder on the right side up to 70 mm in the AP dimension.

Hepatomegaly and fatty liver infiltration. Ascites. Otherwise, as described.

translation:
CT of the Chest

The examination was performed using spiral technique with 2.5 mm slice thickness and reconstructed to 1.2 mm slices.

Examination Description:

Post-surgical changes after resection of approximately 10 cm of the posterior segment of the left sixth rib. There is a spindle-shaped extrapleural hematoma and chest wall hematoma measuring 61x94x150 mm (transverse x sagittal x longitudinal dimensions) extending along the left axillary line from the fourth to the eighth rib. Within it, there are gas bubbles and a calcified area measuring 17x3.5 mm. Smaller hematomas are present in the left lateral chest wall with intermuscular emphysema and subcutaneous fluid reaction. Free fluid is noted in the left pleural cavity with separation up to 7 cm below and above the extrapleural hematoma at the posterior chest wall. There is compressive atelectasis of most of the left lower lobe. A small amount of fluid is present in the right pleural cavity with a pleural thickness up to 9 mm at the posterior wall, with minor compressive and positional atelectasis of the posterior segments of the right lower lobe. Mild mediastinal emphysema and at the base of the neck on the left side. Secretions are noted along the posterior wall of the cervical trachea.

Conclusions:

Status post partial resection of the sixth rib. Extrapleural and chest wall hematoma on the left side. Free fluid in the left pleural cavity with compressive atelectasis of most of the left lower lobe.

translation:
Abdominal Ultrasound

The examination was performed using a Hitachi device.

Examination Description:

The liver shows homogeneous, slightly increased echogenicity due to fatty infiltration, with no distinct focal lesions. The anteroposterior dimension of the right lobe in the midclavicular line is 12.1 cm. Status post-cholecystectomy. The liver hilum is obscured by intestinal gas. The portal vessels and hepatic veins are not dilated within the visible range. The kidneys are in their typical position, of normal size, with preserved corticomedullary differentiation. The right kidney measures 11.1 x 5.4 cm, with a parenchymal thickness of 1.5 cm, slightly thinned at the upper pole. The lower pole of the right kidney is partially unreadable. An eccentric cyst with a parietal septum, measuring up to approximately 4 cm, is present near the upper pole of the right kidney. In the mid-upper calyces of the right kidney, a hyperechoic stone measuring 1.4 cm is visible, with possibly a few small stones nearby. Within the right renal sinus, there are features of several small peripelvic cysts. The left kidney measures 10.3 x 4.9 cm, with a parenchymal thickness of 10 mm. In the central part of the left kidney, there are single stones up to 5 mm in size. Features of single peripelvic cysts are present in the left kidney, measuring up to 0.5 cm. The pancreas is visible in the body region—homogeneous, not enlarged, otherwise obscured by intestinal gas. The spleen is homogeneous, not enlarged, with a bipolar dimension of 8.5 cm. The abdominal aorta is not dilated within the visible range. The urinary bladder is well-filled with urine, anechoic, and thin-walled. The uterus is poorly visualized in the examination. No free fluid is observed in the extraperitoneal or intraperitoneal spaces.

Nieco zwiększona ilość płynu w pochewce nerwu wzrokowego przed zmianą. Zmian obrzękowych i naciekowych wokół opisywanej struktury nie stwierdza się. Nerw wzrokowy lewy poza zmianą w kierunku skrzyżowania nerwów wzrokowych węższy w porównaniu ze stroną prawą. Skrzyżowanie nerwów wzrokowych w normie. Obraz mięśni okoruchowych, gruczołów łzowych i gałek ocznych obustronnie w granicach normy. Po dożylnym podaniu kontrastu nie uwidoczniono obszarów patologicznego wzmocnienia.

Wnioski: Zmiana ogniskowa w rzucie przebiegu nerwu wzrokowego lewego może odpowiadać malformacji jamistej żylnej. W porównaniu z badaniem poprzednim widoczna ewolucja zmian po krwawieniu do malformacji.
translation:
Orbital MRI Report

The examination was performed using T2 FLAIR, T2 FS, T1 in the transverse plane, T2 FS, T1 FS in the coronal plane, T2 in the sagittal plane, and post-contrast T1 FS in the transverse, sagittal, and coronal planes.

Referral information: Evaluation for NMO.

Examination description: The left optic nerve, approximately 11 mm from the posterior pole of the eyeball, shows a distinct lesion measuring 8 x 7 x 6 mm, with smooth, regular margins and features of sedimentation of contents with signal intensities that may correspond to hemoglobin metabolites. There is a slightly increased amount of fluid in the optic nerve sheath before the lesion. No edema or infiltrative changes are observed around the described structure. The left optic nerve, apart from the lesion, is narrower towards the optic chiasm compared to the right side. The optic chiasm is normal. The appearance of the extraocular muscles, lacrimal glands, and eyeballs is within normal limits bilaterally. No areas of pathological enhancement were observed after intravenous contrast administration.

Conclusions: The focal lesion along the course of the left optic nerve may correspond to a cavernous venous malformation. Compared to the previous examination, there is visible evolution of changes following hemorrhage into the malformation.

translation:
MRI of the Head with Contrast

The examination was performed using T1 3D, T2, DWI, T2* sequences in the axial plane, and T2 sequence in the sagittal plane, as well as post-contrast enhancement with FLAIR, T1 3D in the axial plane, and FLAIR in the sagittal plane.

Referral information: Please perform an MRI of the head and compare it with the previous study. Demyelinating syndrome.

Comparison was made with the previous head MRI. Extensive, poorly defined, confluent areas of neurodegenerative changes are noted, involving the periventricular, subcortical, and deep white matter in the supratentorial region, with irregular malacic areas visible adjacent to the ventricular system. Faint abnormal signals are also visible in the pons and middle cerebellar peduncles, without features of focal lesions. The location and morphology of the changes are similar to those in the study dated April 17, 2012. No active areas are visible. The signal intensity of the brain's gray matter is normal. The supratentorial ventricular system is not displaced, enlarged, and symmetrical; the third ventricle is approximately 1 cm wide, as previously noted. The cerebral aqueduct is normal, and the fourth ventricle is moderately wide. There is atrophic deepening of the cerebral sulci and grooves. No areas of pathological diffusion restriction are observed. After intravenous administration of contrast, no areas of pathological signal intensity enhancement are detected. Minor mucosal changes in the ethmoid cells and maxillary sinuses.

Conclusions: MRI of the brain structures shows pronounced demyelinating and neurodegenerative changes—comparable to the study from May 14, 2012, with no signs of activity.

translation:
MRI of the Lumbosacral Spine

The examination was performed using T1, T2, and STIR sequences in the sagittal plane and T2 in the axial plane.

Referral information: Back pain in the lumbosacral region radiating to the left buttock.

Examination description: The alignment of the lumbar spine is normal. There is a flattening of the physiological lumbar lordosis. Sacralization of the L5 vertebra is noted. There is a decreased signal and height of the L4/L5 intervertebral disc, with small osteophytes on the edges of the adjacent vertebral bodies and subchondral signal changes of MODIC type 1. The remaining vertebral bodies and intervertebral discs are of normal height, shape, and signal. Mild degenerative changes due to overload are present in the facet joints, increasing caudally. At the L4/L5 level, there is a broad-based left-sided disc bulge, along with arthropathic changes, causing narrowing of the left lateral recess and intervertebral foramen, with molding and suspected compression of the spinal nerve roots and structures in the root canal. The conus medullaris at the Th12/L1 level is of normal thickness and signal intensity.

Conclusions: Features of a transitional vertebra - sacralization of L5. Discopathy at L4/L5 with suspected compression of the left spinal nerve roots.

translation:
HRCT of the lungs was performed with a 1.25 mm slice thickness, multiphasic, with intravenous contrast enhancement.

Referral data: Chronic cough, chronic sinusitis, shortness of breath. No previous studies available for comparison.

Examination description: Fibrotic consolidations are visible medially in the right middle lobe and the lingula of the left lung. Fibrotic changes in the left apex. Fibrotic-atelectatic changes in the paravertebral gutter in the right lower lobe and subdiaphragmatically on both sides. The bronchial tree is patent. Slight thickening of the bronchial walls, mainly in the lower parts. Small vascular-bronchial bundles with subtly disturbed architecture due to fibrotic-atelectatic changes. Scattered micronodular and small nodular changes up to 4 mm in diameter, with a non-specific appearance. Slight mosaic pattern in the lower parts of the lungs, with small areas of air trapping. The aorta and pulmonary arteries are not dilated, calcifications in the walls of the aorta and coronary arteries. The heart is not enlarged. Calcifications in the area of the aortic valve. Mediastinal lymph nodes are not enlarged. Assessment of the hilar lymph nodes is difficult in the survey study, they appear not enlarged. Abdominal organs are partially included in the study range. Thickening of the lateral limb of the right adrenal gland with a nodule measuring approximately 8x16 mm, with a density in the survey phase of approximately -10 HU, appearing benign. Additionally, a pinpoint calcification is visible in the right adrenal gland. Status post cholecystectomy. The hepatic flexure of the colon lies between the abdominal wall and the liver surface - an anatomical variant. Small hiatal hernia. Degenerative changes in the thoracic spine. Increased thoracic kyphosis.

Conclusions: Fibrotic-atelectatic changes, single small nodular changes in both lungs. Minor bronchiectasis and thickening of the bronchial walls. Otherwise, as described.

Badanie TK mózgowia wykonane bez dożylnego podania środka kontrastowego warstwami 2,5 i 0,6 mm w trybie pilnym/ostrodyżurowym.

Dane ze skierowania: Proszę o ocenę TK głowy. Niedowład kończyny górnej lewej od rana. Otępienie.

Opis badania: Obustronnie, zarówno w strukturach nad- jak i podnamiotowych mózgowia widoczne są dość liczne ogniska hiperdensyjne o zróżnicowanej morfologii- dominuje wzór zmiany obrączkowatej o średnicy od 5 do 18 mm. Największe ze zmian zlokalizowane są w prawym płacie ciemieniowym o bardziej niejednorodnej strukturze niż pozostałe zmiany - ujawnia się "nidus" w środku zmiany obrączkowatej. Wokół tych zmian przylega strefa obrzęku. Rozległe zmiany hypodensyjne w lewym płacie potylicznym oraz mniejsze obszary w prawym płacie czołowym i prawym płacie potylicznym, z nakładającymi się na tym tle jamami malacyjnymi jako wyraz zmian wstecznych. Niewielkie ogniska lakularne w strukturach głębokich mózgu. Pogłębienie i poszerzenie bruzd mózgowia i szczelin móżdżku. Przestrzenie płynowe przymózgowe nieposzerzone. Układ komorowy nadnamiotowy nieprzemieszczony, poszerzony, dość symetryczny. Komora III. szerokości do 13 mm. Blaszki miażdżycowe wewnątrzczaszkowych odcinków ICA oraz VA. Co najmniej dwa hipodensyjne/osteolityczne ogniska w kościach pokrywy czaszki. Mierna hiperostoza kości czołowej. Poza tym struktury kostne bez innych zmian, w tych pourazowych. Zmiany śluzówkowe prawej zatoki szczękowej.

Wnioski: Obraz zmian w mózgowiu sugeruje w pierwszej kolejności obecność zmian metastatycznych. Nie można wykluczyć wtórnego ukrwotocznienia pojedynczych, większych zmian w płacie ciemieniowym po stronie prawej. Hipodensyjne ogniska w kościach pokrywy czaszki o charakterze zmian meta. Rozległe zmiany wsteczne - w pierwszej kolejności zmiany wsteczne naczyniopochodne, do różnicowania ze zmianami pourazowymi. Ewentualne określenia metabolitów krwi w w/w zmianach w MR.
translation:
CT scan of the brain performed urgently without intravenous contrast, with slices of 2.5 and 0.6 mm.

Referral information: Please evaluate the head CT. Left upper limb weakness since morning. Dementia.

Examination description: Numerous hyperdense lesions with varied morphology are visible bilaterally in both supratentorial and infratentorial brain structures. The predominant pattern is ring-shaped lesions ranging from 5 to 18 mm in diameter. The largest lesions are located in the right parietal lobe, exhibiting a more heterogeneous structure than the other lesions, with a "nidus" visible in the center of the ring-shaped lesion. There is an adjacent zone of edema around these lesions. Extensive hypodense changes in the left occipital lobe and smaller areas in the right frontal and right occipital lobes, with overlapping malacic cavities indicating regressive changes. Small lacunar foci in the deep brain structures. Deepening and widening of the cerebral sulci and cerebellar fissures. Pericerebral fluid spaces are not enlarged. The supratentorial ventricular system is not displaced, enlarged, and fairly symmetrical. The third ventricle measures up to 13 mm in wiRXh. Atherosclerotic plaques in the intracranial segments of the ICA and VA. At least two hypodense/osteolytic foci in the skull bones. Mild hyperostosis of the frontal bone. Otherwise, no other changes in the bony structures, including post-traumatic changes. Mucosal changes in the right maxillary sinus.

Conclusions: The appearance of the brain lesions primarily suggests the presence of metastatic changes. Secondary hemorrhagic transformation of individual larger lesions in the right parietal lobe cannot be excluded. Hypodense foci in the skull bones are characteristic of metastatic changes. Extensive regressive changes, primarily vascular in origin, should be differentiated from post-traumatic changes. Possible determination of blood metabolites in the aforementioned changes in MRI.

report:
:



Dane ze skierowania: Podejrzenie przerzutów do OUN z ukrwotocznieniem. Proszę o potwierdzenie/ wykluczenie jw.

Opis badania:

Dokonano korelacji z dostępnym w systemie szpitalnym badaniem TK głowy. W prawym płacie ciemieniowym, w istocie białej podkorowej widoczna jest owalna, dobrze odgraniczona struktura, wymiarów 19 x 16 x 20 mm (ap x sd x cc), o niejednorodnych sygnałach w sekwencji T1, z hiperintensywną obwódką, z widocznymi obszarami ograniczenia dyfuzji w DWI. W przyleganiu do niej, ku tyłowi i przyśrodkowo wyodrębnia się kolejna, niejednorodna, bardziej hipointensywna zmiana ogniskowa wymiarów 15 x 10 x 16 mm (ap x sd x cc). Wokół zmian zaznaczony jest obszar obrzęku wazogennego o separacji do 15 mm. Podobna zmiana o wymiarze na skanach poprzecznych 16 x 9 mm zlokalizowana jest w prawej półkuli mózdżku. Opisywane struktury odpowiadają ukrwotocznionym zmianom o charakterze meta. Zmiany malacyjne w prawym płacie czołowym o wymiarach 28 x 13 mm oraz w lewym płacie ciemieniowym o wymiarach 69 x 28 mm. Dwie jamy malacyjne w prawym płacie czołowym średnicy 7 i 8 mm, z widocznym wokół obszarem obrzęku wazogennego o separacji do 6 mm. Zmiany lakunarne/ naczyniopochodne w jądrach korowo-podkorowych obustronnie. Cechy uogólnionych zaników korowo-podkorowych. Układ komorowy nadnamiotowo dość symetryczny, nieprzemieszczony, poszerzony wtórnie do zaników mózgowia, zwłaszcza w zakresie rogów potylicznych, komora III szerokości do 13 mm. Wodociąg bez patologicznych sygnałów. Komora IV prawidłowa. Przestrzenie przymózgowe poszerzone, wtórnie do zaników tkanki mózgowia. W warstwie korowej prawego płata ciemieniowego w sąsiedztwie zmian ogniskowych widoczny jest półkulisty obszar ograniczonej dyfuzji w DWI, na długości około 35 mm - w pierwszej kolejności jako wynik zmian obrzękowych wokół zmian meta. Poza tym innych obszarów ograniczenie dyfuzji w DWI nie stwierdza się. Zmiany zapalne śluzówki prawej zatoki szczękowej.

Wnioski:

Ukrwotocznione zmiany meta w obrębie mózgowia. Cechy zaników korowo-podkorowych, zmiany malacyjne w obrębie półkul mózgu. Zmiany zapalne prawej zatoki szczękowej. Poza tym jak w opisie badania.
translation:
Referral Data: Suspected metastases to the central nervous system with hemorrhagic transformation. Please confirm or rule out as above.

Examination Description:

Correlation was made with the available CT scan of the head in the hospital system. In the right parietal lobe, within the subcortical white matter, there is an oval, well-defined structure measuring 19 x 16 x 20 mm (ap x sd x cc), with heterogeneous signals on the T1 sequence, featuring a hyperintense rim and areas of diffusion restriction visible on DWI. Adjacent to it, posteriorly and medially, there is another heterogeneous, more hypointense focal lesion measuring 15 x 10 x 16 mm (ap x sd x cc). Surrounding these lesions is an area of vasogenic edema extending up to 15 mm. A similar lesion measuring 16 x 9 mm on transverse scans is located in the right cerebellar hemisphere. The described structures correspond to hemorrhagic metastatic lesions. Malacic changes are noted in the right frontal lobe measuring 28 x 13 mm and in the left parietal lobe measuring 69 x 28 mm. Two malacic cavities in the right frontal lobe with diameters of 7 and 8 mm, with surrounding vasogenic edema extending up to 6 mm. Lacunar/vascular changes are present in the bilateral cortico-subcortical nuclei. Features of generalized cortico-subcortical atrophy are observed. The supratentorial ventricular system is fairly symmetrical, non-displaced, and enlarged secondary to brain atrophy, especially in the occipital horns, with the third ventricle measuring up to 13 mm in wiRXh. The aqueduct shows no pathological signals. The fourth ventricle is normal. The pericerebral spaces are enlarged, secondary to brain tissue atrophy. In the cortical layer of the right parietal lobe, adjacent to the focal changes, there is a hemispherical area of diffusion restriction on DWI, approximately 35 mm in length, primarily as a result of edema changes around the metastatic lesions. No other areas of diffusion restriction on DWI are noted. Inflammatory changes in the mucosa of the right maxillary sinus.

Conclusions:

Hemorrhagic metastatic changes within the brain. Features of cortico-subcortical atrophy, malacic changes within the cerebral hemispheres. Inflammatory changes in the right maxillary sinus. Otherwise, as described in the examination.

report:
:



MR głowy w protokole udarowym. Badanie wykonano w sekwencjach FLAIR, DWI, GRE w płaszczyźnie poprzecznej.

Dane ze skierowania: Podejrzenie udaru mózgu. Pacjent zgłasza niedowład kończyny górnej prawej. Stan po udarze mózgu z niedowładem lewostronnym 03.2021 r.

Opis badania:

W obrębie bruzdy przedśrodkowej okolicy sklepienia lewej półkuli mózgu widoczny jest niewielki obszar wysokich sygnałów w sekwencji DWI, z towarzyszącym obniżeniem sygnałów na mapie ADC; obszar o podobnym charakterze wielkości ok. 5,5 mm obecny także w okolicy bieguna czołowego lewej półkuli mózgu. Obraz sugeruje obecność świeżych ognisk udarowych z zakresu unaczynienia końcowych gałęzi lewej tętnicy środkowej mózgu. W obrębie istoty białej obu półkul widoczne hiperintensywne obszary o lokalizacji podkorowej, okołokomorowej jak w przypadku zmian neurodegeneracyjnych i leukoarajozy. W sąsiedztwie trzonu komory bocznej prawej widoczne są nieliczne obszary bezsygnałowe, otoczone strefą blizny glejowej, odpowiadające zmianom lakunarnym - największa z nich mierzy do około 7mm. Układ komorowy nadnamiotowy poszerzony, nieprzemieszczony, symetryczny, komora III szerokości 13mm. W sekwencjach gradientowych metabolitów hemoglobiny w obrębie mózgowia nie stwierdza się. Dokładniejsza ocena mózgowia w pełnym protokole badania z kontrastem. Innych zmian nie stwierdza się.

Wnioski:

Świeże ogniska udarowe z zakresu unaczynienia dystalnych gałęzi LMCA.
translation:
MRI of the head using a stroke protocol. The examination was performed with FLAIR, DWI, and GRE sequences in the transverse plane.

Referral information: Suspected stroke. The patient reports weakness in the right upper limb. History of stroke with left-sided weakness in March 2021.

Examination description:

A small area of high signal intensity is visible in the DWI sequence within the precentral gyrus region of the left cerebral hemisphere, accompanied by a corresponding low signal on the ADC map. A similar area, approximately 5.5 mm in size, is also present near the frontal pole of the left cerebral hemisphere. The image suggests the presence of acute ischemic foci within the vascular territory of the distal branches of the left middle cerebral artery. Hyperintense areas are visible in the white matter of both hemispheres, located subcortically and periventricularly, consistent with neurodegenerative changes and leukoaraiosis. Adjacent to the body of the right lateral ventricle, there are a few signal void areas surrounded by a zone of gliotic scarring, corresponding to lacunar changes, the largest measuring up to approximately 7 mm. The supratentorial ventricular system is enlarged, non-displaced, symmetrical, with the third ventricle measuring 13 mm in wiRXh. No hemoglobin metabolites are detected in the brain parenchyma on gradient sequences. A more detailed assessment of the brain is recommended with a full contrast-enhanced study. No other changes are noted.

Conclusions:

Acute ischemic foci within the vascular territory of the distal branches of the left middle cerebral artery.

report:
:



MR śródpiersia. Badanie wykonano w sekwencji T2, T2 FS, T1 FS, T1 w płaszczyźnie poprzecznej oraz po dożylnym podaniu środka kontrastowego w sekwencji T1 w płaszczyźnie poprzecznej i strzałkowej.

Dane ze skierowania: Podejrzenie atypowo położonego grasiczaka. Miastenia ciężka, rzekomoporaźna.

Opis badania:

W tkance tłuszczowej lewego kąta przeponowo-sercowego widoczny policykliczny obszar płynowy o łącznych wymiarach 24 x 10 x 27 mm (AP x SD x CC). Sygnały zmiany sugerują bogatobiałkową zawartość. W zakresie zmiany nie stwierdza się ewidentnego pokontrastowego wzmocnienia. Powiększonych węzłów chłonnych śródpiersia nie uwidoczniono. W anatomicznym rzucie grasicy jednorodna tkanka tłuszczowa.

Wnioski:

Uzyskany obraz MR zgodnie z danymi ze skierowania może sugerować obecność drobnego grasiczaka torbielowatego w lewym kącie przeponowo-sercowym. W różnicowaniu można uwzględnić zmiany wsteczne w węzłach chłonnych. Do rozważenia potwierdzenie rozpoznania w badaniu PET/PET-CT.
translation:
Mediastinal MRI. The examination was performed using T2, T2 FS, T1 FS, T1 sequences in the transverse plane, and after intravenous administration of contrast agent in T1 sequences in the transverse and sagittal planes.

Referral information: Suspected atypically located thymoma. Severe, pseudoparalytic myasthenia.

Examination description:

In the adipose tissue of the left cardiophrenic angle, a polycyclic fluid area is visible, measuring 24 x 10 x 27 mm (AP x TR x CC). The signal characteristics of the lesion suggest a high-protein content. There is no evident post-contrast enhancement within the lesion. No enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes are observed. The anatomical projection of the thymus shows homogeneous adipose tissue.

Conclusions:

The obtained MRI image, in accordance with the referral data, may suggest the presence of a small cystic thymoma in the left cardiophrenic angle. Differential diagnosis may include regressive changes in the lymph nodes. Consideration should be given to confirming the diagnosis with a PET/PET-CT scan.

report:
:



TK klatki piersiowej. Badanie wykonano warstwą grubości 2,5, 1,2, 0,6 mm, przed i po dożylnym podaniu (bez wczesnych powikłań) 70 ml środka kontrastującego Ultravist 370.

Dane kliniczne: Sarkoidoza. W RTG niewykluczona zmiana ogniskowa, guzkowa płucna lub węzłowa na wysokości dolnego bieguna prawej wnęki płucnej przyśródpiersiowo, proszę o ocenę.

Opis badania:

Pierwsze badanie TK w systemie szpitalnym RIS.

W płucach rozproszone, nieliczne zagęszczenia drobnoguzkowe obwodowo i podopłucnowo położone. Największy, klinowaty podopłucnowy guzek w segmencie 8 prawym wielkości do 7 mm. Poza tym płuca, drzewo tchawiczo-oskrzelowe niezmienione.

W śródpiersiu zwiększonej ilości i powiększenia węzłów chłonnych nie stwierdza się. Największy z węzłów chłonnych w grupie V do 7 mm w osi krótkiej. W zwiększonej ilości węzły chłonne grupy XI i XII, największe po stronie prawej w osi krótkiej do 10 mm, granicznej wielkości. Drobne węzły chłonne oskrzelowo-płucne przy pęczkach naczyniowo-oskrzelowych płatów dolnych.

Blaszki opłucnej niepogrubiałe. Płynu w jamach opłucnowych, w worku osierdziowym nie stwierdza się.

Serce niepowiększone.

Duże naczynia śródpiersia nieposzerzone, prawidłowo drożne.

Ujęte badaniem narządy nadbrzusza poza obniżeniem stłuszczeniowym gęstości wątroby do ok. 38-42 j.H. zmian nie ujawniają.

Układ kostny bez złośliwej przebudowy struktury. Zmiany zwyrodnieniowe, głównie trzonowe odcinka piersiowego kręgosłupa.

Wnioski:

Nieliczne rozproszone zagęszczenia mikroguzkowe w płucach oraz jeden pojedynczy guzek podopłucnowo położony do 7 mm. Zwiększenie ilości węzłów chłonnych wnęk i oskrzelowopłucnych, bez ich powiększenia. Przy zgodnych danych klinicznych sarkoidoza. Spondyloza piersiowa.
translation:
CT of the chest. The examination was performed with slice thicknesses of 2.5, 1.2, and 0.6 mm, before and after intravenous administration (without early complications) of 70 ml of Ultravist 370 contrast agent.

Clinical data: Sarcoidosis. A focal, nodular pulmonary or nodal lesion at the level of the lower pole of the right pulmonary hilum near the mediastinum was not excluded on X-ray; please evaluate.

Examination description:

First CT examination in the hospital RIS system.

In the lungs, there are scattered, few small nodular opacities located peripherally and subpleurally. The largest, wedge-shaped subpleural nodule in the right segment 8 measures up to 7 mm. Otherwise, the lungs and tracheobronchial tree are unremarkable.

No increased number or enlargement of lymph nodes in the mediastinum is observed. The largest lymph node in group V measures up to 7 mm in short axis. There is an increased number of lymph nodes in groups XI and XII, the largest on the right side measuring up to 10 mm in short axis, at the borderline size. Small bronchopulmonary lymph nodes are present near the vascular-bronchial bundles of the lower lobes.

The pleural layers are not thickened. No fluid is detected in the pleural cavities or pericardial sac.

The heart is not enlarged.

The major mediastinal vessels are not dilated and are patent.

The abdominal organs included in the examination do not reveal changes, except for a reduction in hepatic density due to steatosis to approximately 38-42 HU.

The skeletal system shows no malignant structural remodeling. Degenerative changes, mainly in the thoracic spine.

Conclusions:

Few scattered micronodular opacities in the lungs and a single subpleural nodule up to 7 mm. Increased number of hilar and bronchopulmonary lymph nodes, without enlargement. Consistent with clinical data for sarcoidosis. Thoracic spondylosis.

report:
:



TK klatki piersiowej. Badanie wykonano przed i po podaniu środka kontrastowego (70 ml Ultravistu 370), warstwą 1 mm.

Dane ze skierowania: Sarkoidoza, w poprzednich badaniach stopień II. W RTG klp wysycenia guzkowe i pasmowate o niewielkiej progresji w porównaniu z poprzednim badaniem, nieco większa konsolidacja nadprzeponowo obustronnie. Kontrola.

Opis badania:

Brak badań poprzednich do porównania.

W obrazie obu płuc dominują rozsiane zagęszczenia guzkowe, częściowo zlewające się, lokalizujące się podopłucnowo, w tym także wzdłuż szczelin międzypłatowych oraz przyśródpiersiowo. Opisywane zmiany towarzyszą również biegnącym odwnękowo oraz widocznym na obwodzie płuc pasmom śródmiąższowym - zmianom włóknistym. W obrębie opisywanych zmian guzkowych widoczne są nieliczne zwapnienia.

Odmiana anatomiczna: po stronie lewej widoczna szczelina pozioma.

W obrębie miernie poszerzonych wnęk płuc widoczne są węzły chłonne o zatartych obrysach, zlewajace się.

W obrębie śródpiersia widoczne są dość liczne, lokalnie tworzące pakiety, węzły chłonne, mierzące w osi krótkiej do około 13 mm, w ich obrębie widoczne pojedyncze zwapnienia.

Serce granicznej wielkości.

Duże naczynia klp nieposzerzone.

Poza niewielką torbielą nerki lewej obraz ujętych badaniem narządów nadbrzusza bez uchwytnej patologii.

Ujęte badaniem struktury kostne klp bez cech złośliwej przebudowy.

Wnioski:

W obrazie płuc dominują zmiany guzkowo-włókniste oraz limfadenopatia śródpiersia i wnęk płuc - obraz koreluje z rozpoznaniem.
translation:
CT of the chest. The examination was performed before and after administration of contrast medium (70 ml Ultravist 370), with a 1 mm slice thickness.

Referral information: Sarcoidosis, previously stage II. Chest X-ray showed nodular and band-like opacities with slight progression compared to the previous examination, with somewhat increased consolidation above the diaphragm on both sides. Follow-up.

Examination description:

No previous studies available for comparison.

The imaging of both lungs is dominated by scattered nodular opacities, partially confluent, located subpleurally, including along the interlobar fissures and perihilar regions. These changes are also associated with interstitial bands extending from the hila and visible at the lung periphery - fibrotic changes. Within the described nodular changes, a few calcifications are visible.

Anatomical variant: a horizontal fissure is visible on the left side.

Within the mildly enlarged pulmonary hila, lymph nodes with indistinct borders are visible, merging together.

In the mediastinum, there are numerous lymph nodes, locally forming clusters, measuring up to approximately 13 mm in short axis, with single calcifications visible within them.

The heart is of borderline size.

The major thoracic vessels are not enlarged.

Apart from a small cyst in the left kidney, the image of the upper abdominal organs included in the examination shows no detectable pathology.

The bony structures of the chest included in the examination show no signs of malignant remodeling.

Conclusions:

The lung image is dominated by nodular-fibrotic changes and mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy - the image correlates with the diagnosis.

report:
:



TK mózgowia. Badanie wykonano sekwencyjnie warstwą grubości 2,5 i 0,6 mm w trybie pilnym w fazie przeglądowej.

Dane ze skierowania: Udar niedokrwienny prawej półkuli mózgu.

Opis badania:

Świeże, dokonane zmiany niedokrwienne w fazie obrzęku wazogennego w płacie czołowym i w przyśrodkowo-przedniej części płata skroniowego z częściowym objęciem struktur głębokich prawej półkul mózgu na obszarze około 62 x 50 mm, bez cech ukrwotocznienia.

W obrębie istoty białej nadnamiotowej przewlekłe zmiany wsteczne naczyniopochodnych.

Poza tym gęstość tkankowa istoty szarej oraz białej mózgu w normie.

Trzon prawej komory bocznej miernie modelowany i umiarkowanie przewężony przez obrzękowe zmiany niedokrwienne.

Struktury pośrodkowe nieprzemieszczone.

Wodociąg mózgu i komora IV w normie.

Elementy tylnojamowe patologii nie wykazują.

Przestrzenie płynowe przymózgowe nieposzerzone.

Blaszki miażdżycowe wewnątrzczaszkowych odcinków ICA.

Nadal obecny objaw hyperdensyjnej w części M1 lewej MCA.

Struktury kostne bez patologicznej przebudowy.

Wnioski: Dokonane zmiany niedokrwienne w fazie obrzęku wazogennego bez cech ukrwotocznienia w zakresie części zaopatrzenia gałęzi końcowych i głębokich prawej MCA. Poza tym, jak w opisie powyżej.
translation:
CT of the brain. The examination was performed sequentially with slice thicknesses of 2.5 and 0.6 mm on an urgent basis in the survey phase.

Referral information: Ischemic stroke of the right cerebral hemisphere.

Examination description:

Recent ischemic changes in the vasogenic edema phase in the frontal lobe and the medial-anterior part of the temporal lobe, partially involving the deep structures of the right cerebral hemisphere, measuring approximately 62 x 50 mm, without signs of hemorrhagic transformation.

Chronic vascular-related regressive changes in the supratentorial white matter.

Otherwise, the tissue density of the gray and white matter of the brain is normal.

The body of the right lateral ventricle is moderately shaped and moderately narrowed by ischemic edematous changes.

Midline structures are not displaced.

The cerebral aqueduct and the fourth ventricle are normal.

No pathological findings in the posterior fossa elements.

The cerebrospinal fluid spaces are not enlarged.

Atherosclerotic plaques in the intracranial segments of the ICA.

Persistent hyperdense sign in the M1 segment of the left MCA.

Bone structures show no pathological remodeling.

Conclusions: Completed ischemic changes in the vasogenic edema phase without signs of hemorrhagic transformation in the area supplied by the terminal and deep branches of the right MCA. Otherwise, as described above.

report:
:



TK klatki piersiowej w algorytmie niskodawkowym. Badanie wykonano w fazie przeglądowej warstwa grubości 1,25/2,5 mm.

Dane kliniczne: Ciało obce w przełyku? drzewa oskrzelowego? Połknięta pinezka.

Opis badania:

W drzewie oskrzelowym lewego płuca obecna pinezka. Część pokryta plastikiem/tworzywem sztucznym długości około 11.5 mm tkwi w podziale oskrzela głównego lewego i w oskrzelu górnopłatowym lewym, część metaliczna niepokryta plastikiem długości około 9.5 mm położona w dalszym odcinku oskrzela głównego lewego.

Poza tym obraz narządów klatki piersiowej w wykonanym badaniu prawidłowy.
translation:
Low-dose CT scan of the chest. The examination was performed in a survey phase with slice thickness of 1.25/2.5 mm.

Clinical data: Foreign body in the esophagus? Bronchial tree? Swallowed pin.

Examination description:

A pin is present in the bronchial tree of the left lung. translation:
CT scan of the chest with HRCT performed in 1.25 mm slices.

Examination description:

Left-sided pneumothorax at the apex measuring up to 23 mm. Larger pneumothorax on the right side measuring up to 40 mm in the lower anterior part of the lung.

On this background, multiple cystic structures are predominantly distributed from the apex to the lung bases, bilaterally, with a predominance in the upper-middle parts. Some peripheral areas measure up to 5 cm. In the basal parts, especially of the right lung, there are consolidations resembling thickened interlobular septa, partially atelectatic due to compression, particularly in the lower parts of the right lung. The overall image suggests significantly reduced ventilation. In the right pleural cavity, a small amount of free fluid with separation up to 10 mm extends into the interlobar fissure, and at the site of the pneumothorax, it forms a level.

The left pleural cavity is free of fluid.

Single drains are visible in both pleural cavities, on the right with the tip at the base of the lung anteriorly, on the left - posteriorly.

Mediastinal emphysema. Extensive subcutaneous emphysema in the neck and nape area included in the examination, as well as the chest wall.

Within the mediastinum and pulmonary hila, lymph nodes are visible but not enlarged.

Major thoracic vessels are properly contrasted, not dilated. The tracheobronchial tree is of normal diameter.

The heart is not enlarged. A trace of fluid in the pericardial sac.

The liver, which is only partially included, appears enlarged. In the remaining area, the included part of the epigastrium shows no evident pathology.

Bone structures show no pathological remodeling.

Conclusions:

Pulmonary histiocytosis. Bilateral pneumothorax. Mediastinal emphysema. Subcutaneous emphysema. Fluid in the right pleural cavity. Atelectatic changes in the right lung.

translation:
CT angiography of the abdominal aorta and iliac vessels was performed using a spiral technique with 1.2mm slices following the intravenous administration of 100ml of non-ionic contrast agent Ultravist 370.

Clinical data: Suspected dissection of the abdominal aorta.

Urgent examination report:

Emphysema and fibrosis areas above the diaphragm.

The descending aorta above the diaphragm is atherosclerotically dilated to 51mm, with mural thrombi up to 12mm thick. The abdominal aorta below the diaphragm measures up to 41mm in wiRXh. The celiac trunk and superior mesenteric artery are properly contrasted. There is a fusiform aneurysm of the abdominal aorta measuring up to 60x53mm, extending approximately 127mm, with a partial rupture of the anterior wall about 47mm above the aortic bifurcation. The average flow lumen within the aneurysm measures approximately 27x23mm. It begins just below the origin of the main right and left renal arteries and extends to the level of the aortic bifurcation. The left kidney is supplied by two renal arteries, with an additional left renal artery originating about 12mm above the main renal artery, supplying its lower pole. Both kidneys have cortical cysts, with the left side measuring up to 31x42mm. The aneurysm is compressing the horizontal part of the duodenum.

Both common and external iliac arteries are atherosclerotically altered but maintain flow despite the presence of mural atherosclerotic plaques. The right external iliac artery is significantly narrowed in its initial segment over a length of approximately 13mm.

The skeletal system shows no pathological destruction.

Conclusions:

Fusiform aneurysm of the abdominal aorta with partial rupture of its anterior wall. Generalized atherosclerotic features. Otherwise, as described above.

Mild quadriceps and patellar tendinosis.

report:
ÉCHOGRAPHIE DU GENOU GAUCHE AVEC BIOPSIE ÉCHOGUIDÉE
 
Histoire clinique : homme de 20 ans avec une masse au genou, pour biopsie
 
Comparaison : IRM du 13 septembre 2024 
 
Résultats :
 
L'évaluation échographique limitée de la partie antérieure du genou gauche démontre une large lésion intra-articulaire dans la région de la graisse de Hoffa. La lésion mesure environ 6,5 x 9,0 x 5,2 cm et présente une échotexture hétérogène et une légère vascularisation interne. Il y a un épanchement intra-articulaire modéré du genou.
 
Procédure : 
 
L'intervention et ses risques potentiels (y compris saignement, infection et dommage aux structures environnantes) ont été expliqués au patient et un consentement éclairé écrit a été obtenu.
 
Une approche médiale a été utilisée, comme demandé par l'oncologue orthopédique référent. 
 
En utilisant une technique stérile, une anesthésie locale avec 1% de lidocaïne a été administrée. Sous guidage échographique, un système de biopsie par carottage de calibre 18 a été introduit dans la lésion. Cinq échantillons ont été prélevés et envoyés en pathologie. 
 
La procédure a été bien tolérée sans complications immédiates.
 
Conclusion :
 
Une biopsie échoguidée de la masse intra-articulaire du genou gauche a été réalisée.
translation:
ULTRASOUND OF THE LEFT KNEE WITH ULTRASOUND-GUIDED BIOPSY
 
Clinical history: 20-year-old male with knee mass, for biopsy
 
Comparison: MRI dated 13 September 2024 
 
Findings:
 
Limited ultrasound evaluation of the anterior aspect of the left knee demonstrates a large intra-articular lesion at the region of Hoffa’s fat pad. The lesion measures approximately 6.5 x 9.0 x 5.2 cm and demonstrates a heterogenous echotexture and mild internal vascularity. There is a moderate knee joint effusion.
 
Procedure: 
 
The procedure and its potential risks (including bleeding, infection, and damage to surrounding structures) were explained to the patient and written informed consent was obtained.
 
A medial approach was used, as requested by the referring orthopedic oncologist. 
 
Using a sterile technique, local anesthesia with 1% lidocaine was administered. Under ultrasound guidance, an 18-gauge core biopsy system was advanced into the lesion. Five samples were obtained and sent to pathology. 
 
The procedure was well tolerated without immediate complications.
 
Conclusion:
 
An ultrasound-guided biopsy of the intra-articular left knee mass was performed.
