Hallazgos. Tejidos blandos periféricos con grosor y densidad adecuados. Estructuras óseas con densidad conservada, esclerosis de las superficies articulares e inicio de formación de osteofitos, con disminución del espacio intersomático; sin evidencia de lesiones líticas, blásticas ni trazos de fracturas. Hígado de tamaño y situación habitual de bordes regulares definidos, parénquima con densidad conservada, sin imágenes solidas ni quísticas. No dilatación de la vía biliar. Vesícula biliar semidistendia. Bazo, Páncreas ambas suprarrenales con situación y morfología habituales, de bordes regulares y bien definidos, parénquima de densidad homogénea sin evidencia de lesiones en su interior. Con presencia de líquido confluente en polo superior de bazo. Estomago semidistensión. Colon con abundante material residual, con sigmoides redundante. Intestino delgado con dilatación y leve engrosamiento de la pared, aparentemente con algunas burbujas en pared. Riñones con situación y morfología habituales, bordes regulares y bien definidos. Parénquima de densidad homogénea. Sistemas pielocaliciales sin dilatación aparente. Estructuras de hueco pélvico de adecuado tamaño y morfología para la edad del paciente sin alteraciones por este método de estudio. Los trayectos vasculares retroperitoneales están bien definidos, con morfología conservada. No adenomegalias.
Conclusión: 
Estudio que muestra datos de ileo no obstructivo, a considerar neumatosis incipiente, se recomienda complementar con estudio contrastado 
Cambios por discoartropatía generalizada
translation:
Reason for Study: Abdominal pain.
Technique: A simple phase study was performed with cuts at the hepatic level and extending to the pelvic cavity.
 
Findings: Soft Tissue peripheral soft tissues with adequate thickness and density.
Bone Structures, conserved density, with sclerosis of joint surfaces and early formation of osteophytes, along with decreased intervertebral space. No evidence of lytic, blastic lesions, or fracture traces.
Liver, normal size and position, with defined regular borders, and preserved parenchyma density. No solid or cystic images observed. No bile duct dilatation.
Gallbladder, semi-distended.
Spleen, normal situation and morphology, with regular and well-defined borders, homogeneous parenchyma density. Presence of confluent fluid in the upper pole of the spleen.
Pancreas, normal situation and morphology, with regular and well-defined borders, homogeneous parenchyma density, with no internal lesions.
Adrenal Glands, both adrenal glands in their normal position and morphology, with regular and well-defined borders, and homogeneous density, without internal lesions.
Stomach, semi-distended.
Colon, abundant residual material with redundant sigmoid colon.
Small Intestine: Dilated with slight wall thickening, with some bubbles in the wall.
Kidneys, normal situation and morphology, with regular and well-defined borders. Homogeneous parenchyma density. No apparent dilation of the pelvicalyceal systems.
Pelvic Cavity Structures, appropriate size and morphology for the patient's age, with no alterations detected by this imaging method.
Retroperitoneal Vascular Structures, well-defined with preserved morphology.
Lymph Nodes, no adenomegaly.
 
Conclusion:
The study shows signs of non-obstructive ileus, with consideration for incipient pneumatosis. It is recommended to complement with a contrast-enhanced study.
Generalized disc arthropathy changes.

report:
Se realizó tomografía computada de abdomen desde las cúpulas diafragmáticas hasta la sínfisis del pubis, en fase simple y contrastada, encontrando: Se observan ambos hemidiafragmas de características normales y se encuentra glándula hepática de morfología general normal, de contornos regulares con densidad homogénea sin evidencia de lesión focal o difusa, con aumento de dimensiones de su lóbulo izquierda y disminución del derecho en forma cualitativa las estructuras vasculares y las vías biliares se observan dentro de la normalidad. No se observan realces focales o difusos. Se identifican formaciones colaterales a nivel periesofágico inferior, en unión gastroesofágica, espleno renales y periportales con realce tras la administración de medio de contraste y disposición serpentiforme, así como recanalización del ligamento falciforme con formaciones colaterales a nivel de pared abdominal anterior Se identifica líquido libre de características hipodensas y homogéneas que ocupa todos los receso supra e infra meso cólicos y hasta hueco pélvico con desplazamiento centripeto de asas intestinales La vesícula biliar se observa en situación anatómica, de morfología piriforme, hipodensa en su interior, homogénea, con halo hipodenso debería vesicular. El páncreas es de morfología normal, de contornos regulares adecuada relación con sus marcadores anatómicos correspondientes a la vena mesentérica superior y a la vena esplénica sin alteraciones en sus diferentes segmentos correspondientes a cabeza cuerpo y cola. El bazo presenta morfología y dimensiones aumentadas con longitud craneocaudal de 14. 9 cm con densidad conservada sin datos aparentes de patología focalizada. Los riñones se encuentran simétricos, de dimensiones normales y parénquima homogéneo en fase simple y contrastada, con algunas imágenes redondeadas hipodensas homogéneas sin realces tras la administración de medio contraste con diámetro de 7 mm dispuestos aleatoriamente en número de tres en riñón derecho y cuatro en riñón izquierdo, con sistemas colectores y pielocaliciales sin dilataciones, ni imágenes en relación con litos. La grasa del seno e hilio renal se observa conservada. Eliminación bilateral simétrica observable.
Los psoas y los músculos dorso-lumbares se encuentran dentro de la normalidad. Los grandes vasos aorta y vena cava inferior son de morfología normal sin datos de compresión sin datos de patologia. Estómago y asas intestinales muestran adecuada tinción por el material de contraste ingerido por vía oral con adecuado desplazamiento y sin imágenes de obstrucción. Colon ascendente, transverso y descendente a moderada repleción con residuo en su interior, aparentemente sin alteraciones. Hacia la región de la pelvis se observa vejiga urinaria de características normales a repleción con líquido en su interior de pared conservada. Las estructuras pélvicas se observan dentro de normalidad. 
 
IMPRESIÓN DIAGNÓSTICA: 
· Los hallazgos en su conjunto sugieren enfermedad hepática difusa a considerar cirrosis hepática asociado a ascitis, esplenomegalia, y formaciones portosistémicas periportales, gastroesofágicas y esplenorrenal es así como el recanalización del ligamento falciforme y colaterales de pared abdominal anterior 
· Edema de pared vesicular secundaria · Quistes Bosniak I bilaterales 
· Resto del estudio sin alteraciones. Se sugiere complementar con ecografía Doppler de hígado y vías biliares
translation:
Procedure: Computed tomography of the abdomen from the diaphragmatic domes to the pubic symphysis, performed in both plain and contrast-enhanced phases, showing the following:
 
Both hemidiaphragms appear normal. The liver gland shows normal overall morphology, with regular contours and homogeneous density, without evidence of focal or diffuse lesions. There is an increase in the size of the left lobe and a qualitative decrease in the right lobe. The vascular structures and bile ducts appear normal. No focal or diffuse enhancements are observed.
Collateral formations are identified at the lower esophageal level, at the gastroesophageal junction, splenorenal, and periportal areas, with enhancement after contrast medium administration and serpentine disposition, as well as recanalization of the falciform ligament with collateral formations at the anterior abdominal wall level.
Free fluid with hypodense and homogeneous characteristics is identified, occupying all supra- and infra-mesocolic recesses and extending to the pelvic cavity, with centripetal displacement of intestinal loops.
The gallbladder is observed in its anatomical position, with a pear-shaped morphology, hypodense interior, homogeneous, with a hypodense halo around it.
The pancreas has a normal morphology, with regular contours and appropriate relation to its anatomical markers, the superior mesenteric vein, and the splenic vein, without alterations in its different segments (head, body, and tail).
The spleen shows increased size with a cranio-caudal length of 14.9 cm and preserved density, with no apparent focal pathology.
The kidneys are symmetrical, with normal dimensions and homogeneous parenchyma in both plain and contrast phases, showing some round, homogeneous hypodense images without enhancement after contrast medium administration, with a diameter of 7 mm, randomly distributed (three in the right kidney and four in the left kidney), with no dilation in the collecting systems or associated with stones. The perirenal fat and hilum are preserved. Bilateral symmetric elimination is observable.
The psoas and dorsal-lumbar muscles are within normal limits. The large vessels, aorta, and inferior vena cava are of normal morphology without signs of compression or pathology.
The stomach and intestinal loops show adequate enhancement from the orally ingested contrast material, with proper displacement and no obstruction.
The ascending, transverse, and descending colon are moderately filled with residual material, apparently without alterations. The urinary bladder in the pelvic region appears normal, filled with liquid, and with preserved wall characteristics. Pelvic structures appear normal.
 
Diagnostic Impression:

translation:
DESCRIPTION:
 The following findings were observed: 
The liver has microlobulated contours with a heterogeneous echotexture of fine granular appearance. There are no focal cystic or solid lesions.
 • Quantitative elastography was performed, obtaining 10 samples from the right lobe with an average shear wave velocity of 1.75 m/s and a median of 1.74 m/s, corresponding to F3 on the Metavir scale. These morphological and elastographic findings suggest advanced compensated chronic liver disease.
 The intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts show no dilation, and the bile duct measures 4.3 mm.
 The gallbladder has normal distension, with a regular wall measuring 2.5 mm, and floating punctate echoes are observed inside.
 The portal vein follows a normal course, and Doppler shows it is patent with hepatopetal flow and a velocity of 20.4 cm/s. The portosplenic axis is patent, and the direction of flow is normal.
 The inferior vena cava and abdominal aorta show no abnormalities. The suprahepatic veins are patent with a normal spectral pattern, and the "a" wave is positive.
 The pancreas has regular contours and homogeneous echogenicity, with no dilation of the Wirsung duct. In the biliopancreatic junction, an oval-shaped lymph node is identified with a preserved echogenic center and regular, though slightly thickened, cortex, measuring 21.8 x 7.3 x 20.3 mm.
 The kidneys are of normal size, with a preserved corticomedullary relationship, and there are no signs of hydronephrosis or lithiasis.
 The spleen has homogeneous echogenicity, measuring 117 x 52 x 63 mm, with a splenic index of 383.
 No free fluid is observed in the abdominal cavity.
 
CONCLUSION:
Morphological and elastographic changes suggest advanced compensated chronic liver disease, with no focal lesions and a patent portal vein. US LI-RADS 1 (negative).
F3 on the Metavir scale by elastography for a patient with chronic liver disease.
Inflammatory benign-looking lymphadenopathy at the biliopancreatic junction.
Punctate echoes in the gallbladder suggestive of cholesterol crystals.

Hallazgos: Hígado en situación habitual, de bordes regulares y bien definidos, aumento global de la ecogenicidad con respecto al parénquima renal que condiciona disminución de la visualización de trayectos vasculares, sin imágenes sólidas ni quísticas en su interior, sin datos de dilatación de la vía biliar intra ni extrahepática. Riñón izquierdo de localización habitual, bordes lobulados, relación corticomedular conservada, medidas de 136 x 53 x 57 mm en sus ejes mayores, adecuada vascularidad al modo Doppler color, sin evidencia de lesiones quísticas, sólidas ni ectasia.

IMPRESIÓN DIAGNÓSTICA: 
Cambios por esteatosis hepática grado II (moderado). 
Pérdida de la morfología renal derecha secundario a bolsa hidronefrótica, no se visualiza sitio de obstrucción, se sugiere estudio complementario de TC abdominal para mayor caracterización.
Crecimiento prostático con volumen de 24.38 cc correspondiente a un grado I (Leve). 
Vejiga de características morfológicas conservadas con vaciamiento total.
Resto del estudio en parámetros de la normalidad.
translation:
ABDOMINAL + PELVIC ULTRASOUND
Technique: An ultrasonographic study was performed on the patient using a multifrequency convex transducer, with real-time grayscale imaging and the application of color Doppler.
 
Findings:
Liver in its usual position, with regular and well-defined borders, global increase in echogenicity compared to the renal parenchyma, which causes reduced visualization of vascular structures. No solid or cystic images are seen inside, and no evidence of dilation in the intra- or extrahepatic biliary ducts. Suprahepatic vessels and portal vein with preserved shape, size, and course. The portal vein measures 10.83 mm. The common bile duct measures 3.53 mm.
Gallbladder is partially distended, with thin walls, anechoic and homogeneous content, measuring 29 x 14 mm in its largest axes. Negative sonographic Murphy's sign.
Pancreas in its usual position, with regular borders, homogeneous echotexture, and measurements of 17.08 x 19.37 mm in the head and body segments. The tail is not visualized due to the interposition of abundant intestinal gas.
Spleen is in its usual location, with regular, well-defined borders, and preserved echogenicity, measuring 116 mm.
Right kidney shows loss of its usual architecture secondary to a hydronephrotic sac, leading to cortical thinning and loss of the cortico-medullary relationship. It measures 187 x 105 x 70 mm in its largest axes.
Left kidney is in its usual location, with lobulated borders and preserved corticomedullary relationship. It measures 136 x 53 x 57 mm in its largest axes, with adequate vascularity on color Doppler. No evidence of cystic, solid lesions, or ectasia.
Bladder is distended, with thin walls, anechoic and homogeneous content, with a volume of 136 cc at the time of the study. Only the right ureteral jet is visualized. Post-void volume of 1.72 cc.
No free fluid is observed in the upper abdomen.
Prostate has an oval morphology, homogeneous parenchyma, and is enlarged, with dimensions of 34 x 37 x 36 mm in its largest axes for a volume of 24.38 cc, with a 4.72 mm impression on the bladder floor.
 
DIAGNOSTIC IMPRESSION:
Changes consistent with grade II (moderate) hepatic steatosis.
Loss of right kidney morphology secondary to a hydronephrotic sac; no obstruction site visualized. A complementary abdominal CT scan is suggested for further characterization.
Prostatic enlargement with a volume of 24.38 cc, corresponding to grade I (mild).
Bladder with preserved morphological characteristics and complete emptying.
The rest of the study shows normal parameters.

The diaphragm is well visualized, with homogeneous echotexture and no focal lesions. The liver measures 14.1 cm in its longitudinal axis. There is no dilation of the intra- or extrahepatic bile ducts at the time of the study. The common bile duct has a diameter of 5.8 mm.
Vascular structures are patent.
The portal vein shows hepatopetal flow with a phasic spectrum, and a maximum systolic velocity of 15.5 cm/sec. It measures 9.9 mm in diameter.
The hepatic artery is patent, with antegrade pulsatile flow, a maximum systolic velocity of 51 cm/sec, and a resistance index of 0.62.
The gallbladder is not visualized due to a previous surgical history.
 
Diagnostic impression:
Moderate diffuse hepatic steatosis.
Post-cholecystectomy changes.

report:
Se realizó tomografía computada de abdomen desde las cúpulas diafragmáticas hasta la sínfisis del
pubis, en fase simple y contrastada, encontrando:
 
Se observan ambos hemidiafragmas de características normales y se encuentra glándula hepática de morfología general normal, de contornos regulares con densidad homogénea sin evidencia de lesión focal o difusa, con aumento de dimensiones de su lóbulo izquierda y disminución del derecho en
forma cualitativa las estructuras vasculares y las vías biliares se observan dentro de la normalidad.
No se observan realces focales o difusos. Se identifican formaciones colaterales a nivel periesofágico
inferior, en unión gastroesofágica, espleno renales y periportales con realce tras la administración de
medio de contraste y disposición serpentiforme, así como recanalización del ligamento falciforme con
formaciones colaterales a nivel de pared abdominal anterior
 
Se identifica líquido libre de características hipodensas y homogéneas que ocupa todos los receso supra e infra meso cólicos y hasta hueco pélvico con desplazamiento centripeto de asas intestinales
La vesícula biliar se observa en situación anatómica, de morfología piriforme, hipodensa en su interior, homogénea, con halo hipodenso debería vesicular.
El páncreas es de morfología normal, de contornos regulares adecuada relación con sus marcadores anatómicos correspondientes a la vena mesentérica superior y a la vena esplénica sin alteraciones en sus diferentes segmentos correspondientes a cabeza cuerpo y cola.
El bazo presenta morfología y dimensiones aumentadas con longitud craneocaudal de 14. 9 cm con
densidad conservada sin datos aparentes de patología focalizada.
Los riñones se encuentran simétricos, de dimensiones normales y parénquima homogéneo en fase simple y contrastada, con algunas imágenes redondeadas hipodensas homogéneas sin realces tras la administración de medio contraste con diámetro de 7 mm dispuestos aleatoriamente en número de tres en riñón derecho y cuatro en riñón izquierdo, con sistemas colectores y pielocaliciales sin dilataciones, ni imágenes en relación con litos. La grasa del seno e hilio renal se observa conservada. 
Eliminación bilateral simétrica observable.
Los psoas y los músculos dorso-lumbares se encuentran dentro de la normalidad.
Los grandes vasos aorta y vena cava inferior son de morfología normal sin datos de compresión sin datos de patologia.
Estómago y asas intestinales muestran adecuada tinción por el material de contraste ingerido por vía oral con adecuado desplazamiento y sin imágenes de obstrucción. Colon ascendente, transverso y descendente a moderada repleción con residuo en su interior, aparentemente sin alteraciones.
Hacia la región de la pelvis se observa vejiga urinaria de características normales a repleción con líquido en su interior de pared conservada.
Las estructuras pélvicas se observan dentro de normalidad.
 
IMPRESIÓN DIAGNÓSTICA:
Los hallazgos en su conjunto sugieren enfermedad hepática difusa a considerar cirrosis hepática
asociado a ascitis, esplenomegalia, y formaciones portosistémicas periportales, gastroesofágicas y
esplenorrenal es así como el recanalización del ligamento falciforme y colaterales de pared abdominal
anterior
Edema de pared vesicular secundaria
Quistes Bosniak I bilaterales
Resto del estudio sin alteraciones.
translation:
A computed tomography (CT) scan of the abdomen was performed from the diaphragmatic domes to the pubic symphysis, in both plain and contrast-enhanced phases, finding the following:
 
Both hemidiaphragms show normal characteristics, and the liver gland has a generally normal morphology, with regular contours, homogeneous density, and no evidence of focal or diffuse lesions. There is an increase in the size of the left lobe and a reduction in the right lobe, observed qualitatively. The vascular structures and bile ducts appear normal.
No focal or diffuse enhancements are observed. Collateral formations are identified at the lower periesophageal level, gastroesophageal junction, splenorenal, and periportal areas, with enhancement after contrast administration and a serpentine pattern. Additionally, recanalization of the falciform ligament is noted, with collateral formations at the level of the anterior abdominal wall.
Free fluid of hypodense, homogeneous characteristics is identified, occupying all the supra- and infra-mesocolic recesses and extending into the pelvic cavity, causing centripetal displacement of intestinal loops.
The gallbladder is in its anatomical position, with a pear-shaped morphology, hypodense and homogeneous content, and a hypodense halo around it.
The pancreas has a normal morphology, regular contours, and an appropriate relationship with its corresponding anatomical markers, including the superior mesenteric vein and the splenic vein, with no alterations in its different segments (head, body, and tail).
The spleen has increased size, with a craniocaudal length of 14.9 cm, with preserved density and no apparent signs of focal pathology.
The kidneys are symmetrical, of normal size, with homogeneous parenchyma in both plain and contrast phases. There are several round, hypodense, homogeneous images, with no enhancement after contrast administration, measuring 7 mm. These are randomly distributed—three in the right kidney and four in the left kidney. The collecting systems and renal pelvis show no dilation, and no evidence of stones is seen. The renal sinus and hilum fat is preserved. Bilateral elimination is symmetrical and observable.
The psoas and dorsolumbar muscles are within normal limits.
The aorta and inferior vena cava are of normal morphology, with no evidence of compression or pathology.
The stomach and intestinal loops show adequate contrast uptake through oral ingestion, with normal transit and no signs of obstruction. The ascending, transverse, and descending colon are moderately filled with residual material, with no apparent abnormalities.
In the pelvic region, the urinary bladder is normal, filled with fluid, and has a preserved wall.
The pelvic structures appear normal.
 
Diagnostic impression:
The findings collectively suggest diffuse liver disease, likely cirrhosis, associated with ascites, splenomegaly, and portosystemic collateral formations in the periportal, gastroesophageal, and splenorenal regions, along with recanalization of the falciform ligament and collateral formations in the anterior abdominal wall.
Gallbladder wall edema secondary to other conditions.
Bilateral Bosniak I renal cysts.
The rest of the study shows no significant abnormalities.

translation:

Mediastinal adenopathies with an inflammatory appearance.

translation:
A CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis was performed with a multidetector in both the non-contrast phase and after the administration of non-ionic contrast medium via intravenous route, covering from both lung bases to the pubic symphysis. The following findings were observed:
Lung bases show adequate aeration.
The liver has a normal shape, size, and position, with homogeneous parenchyma and lobulated margins. The intrahepatic bile ducts have a normal course and caliber.
The portal vein measures 16 mm in thickness. The gallbladder is not evaluable.
The pancreas, adrenal glands, and spleen appear normal.
Free fluid is observed in the perihepatic, peripheral, paracolic gutter, and pelvic regions.
The stomach is slightly distended, with thickened walls measuring up to 19 mm.
The small intestine has a normal course and caliber.
The colonic frame contains a small amount of residual material. Thickening of the colonic wall is noted, measuring up to 12 mm, with mucosal enhancement after contrast administration.
Saccular images are seen along the wall of the sigmoid colon.
The kidneys are of normal shape, size, and position, with homogeneous parenchyma, showing appropriate nephrographic and excretory phases.
The collecting systems appear normal.
The bladder is distended, with homogeneous content and thin walls. The uterus and adnexa are not evaluable.
 
Diagnostic impression:
Findings suggestive of hepatic cirrhosis.
Thickening of the stomach wall of undetermined origin.
Signs of portal hypertension.
Abundant ascites.
Diverticulosis in the sigmoid colon.
The uterus and adnexa are not evaluable.
Calcified atheromatosis.
Spondyloarthrosis.
The rest of the study shows no significant abnormalities.

translation:
DESCRIPTION: 
Free fluid is identified in the abdominal cavity in the supraphrenic space, Morrison's pouch, paracolic gutters, and splenorenal area. The liver appears small in size with irregular, lobulated borders and a "fine granular" echographic pattern. Partial loss of the interface with muscular structures is observed. The gallbladder is partially distended, with a wall thickness of 5.4 mm and anechoic content.
Color and spectral Doppler application to the vascular structures show the suprahepatic veins with a loss of their usual pattern, now monophase. The hepatic artery shows a peak systolic velocity of 102.8 cm/second, along with an increase in the resistance index. The portal vein shows increased echogenicity of its content, with absence of flow, but flow is present at the level of the confluence. The common bile duct shows no abnormalities. The pancreas and kidneys show no evident abnormalities. The spleen has a longitudinal axis of 117.2 mm and a splenic volume of 347 cc.
 
CONCLUSION:
Chronic diffuse liver disease with monophase pattern changes in the spectra of the suprahepatic veins and portal vein thrombosis.
The spleen has a larger-than-usual longitudinal axis, but its splenic volume is preserved.
Ascites.

du 17 07 2024


INDICATION :
Réévaluation après pneumonectomie gauche d'un carcinome bronchique lipidique stade IV en progression après trois lignes de chimiothérapie.

TECHNIQUE :
Acquisition hélicoïdale après injection de contraste iodé
PDC :
DLP crâne : 1014mGy.cm, DLP TAP : 2056mGy.cm

RESULTAT : 
Comparativement au scanner du 01/04/2024 (nouveau scanner base line) :
Lésions cibles :
Cible 1 : Lésion de la languette hépatique gauche de 23 mm versus 12 mm

Lésions non cibles :
Adénomégalie rétrosternale droite de 10 mm stable et adénomégalie du secteur4L  de 12 mm de petit axe stable
Majoration non équivoque des micronodules restant de petit axe compris entre 3 et 5 mm disséminés au sein du champ pulmonaire droit
Majoration non équivoque de la lésion lytique de l'aile iliaque gauche avec une lésion de 5 cm avec envahissement des parties molles adjacentes versus 18 mm
Majoration non équivoque de la lésion lytique du plateau vertébral supérieur de L2
Globale stabilité de la fracture pathologique de la 7e côte droite
Majoration non équivoque de la lésion pontique paramédiane droite mesurant 7 mm versus 4 mm. Cette majoration n'est pas interprétable compte tenu du traitement récent

Nouvelles lésions :
Apparition de nouvelles lésions suspectes hépatiques bilobaires (huit nouvelles lésions la plus volumineuse de 17 mm au niveau de la pointe hépatique)
Apparition de nouvelles lésions osseuses lytiques : Corps vertébral de D11, arc moyen de la 4e cote gauche, aile iliaque gauche, tête fémorale gauche. 
Pas de lésion à risque médullaire

Lésion indéterminée :
Infiltrats bronchiolitiques lobaires moyens et lobe supérieur droit avec une plage de condensation sous-pleurale du segment médial du lobe moyen 

Autres constatations :
Thorax :
Témoignage de pneumonectomie gauche. Comblement hydrogazeux de la cavité de pneumonectomie
Fractures en voie de consolidation des 7e et 8e côtes gauches en rapport avec la chirurgie
DVI bracchial gauche avec extrémité du cathéther dans l'oreillette droite sans thrombus sur son trajet.

Abdomen pelvis :
Surrénales fines. Reins respectés. Petite lame d'épanchement dans le Douglas.
Sigmoïdite non compliquée.
Stabilité du kyste biliaire.

Étage encéphalique :
Pas d'autre lésion suspecte.
Pas d'hydrocéphalie. Sinus veineux endocrâniens perméables.


CONCLUSION : 
L'exploration est en faveur d'une progression tumorale avec majoration des lésions cibles et non cibles précédemment décrites et apparition de nouvelles lésions secondaires hépatiques et osseuses.
translation:
Thoraco-abdominal-pelvic and cerebral CT scan
Date: 07/17/2024

INDICATION:
Re-evaluation following left pneumonectomy for stage IV lipidic bronchial carcinoma, progressing after three lines of chemotherapy.

TECHNIQUE:
Helical acquisition post-iodinated contrast injection
CTDI:
Cranial DLP: 1014 mGy.cm, Thoraco-abdominal-pelvic DLP: 2056 mGy.cm

RESULTS:
Compared to the CT scan from 04/01/2024 (new baseline scan):
Target lesions:
Target 1: Lesion in the left hepatic lobe measuring 23 mm compared to 12 mm previously.

Non-target lesions:
Stable right retrosternal adenopathy measuring 10 mm and stable 4L sector adenopathy with a short axis of 12 mm.
Unequivocal increase in remaining micronodules with short axes between 3 and 5 mm scattered throughout the right lung field.
Unequivocal increase in the lytic lesion of the left iliac wing, now measuring 5 cm with adjacent soft tissue invasion compared to 18 mm previously.
Unequivocal increase in the lytic lesion of the superior endplate of L2.
Overall stability of the pathological fracture of the 7th right rib.
Unequivocal increase in the right paramedian pontine lesion measuring 7 mm compared to 4 mm. This increase is not interpretable given recent treatment.

New lesions:
Emergence of new suspicious bilobar hepatic lesions (eight new lesions, the largest being 17 mm at the hepatic tip).
Emergence of new lytic bone lesions: D11 vertebral body, mid-arch of the 4th left rib, left iliac wing, left femoral head.
No lesions posing a risk to the spinal cord.

Indeterminate lesion:
Middle lobar and right upper lobe bronchiolitic infiltrates with a subpleural consolidation area in the medial segment of the middle lobe.

Other findings:
Thorax:
Evidence of left pneumonectomy. Hydroaeric filling of the pneumonectomy cavity.
Healing fractures of the 7th and 8th left ribs related to surgery.
Left brachial DVI with catheter tip in the right atrium without thrombus along its path.

Abdomen pelvis:
Adrenals are thin. Kidneys are preserved. Small fluid collection in the Douglas pouch.
Uncomplicated sigmoiditis.
Stable biliary cyst.

Cerebral region:
No other suspicious lesions.
No hydrocephalus. Intracranial venous sinuses are patent.

CONCLUSION:
The findings suggest tumor progression with an increase in previously described target and non-target lesions and the appearance of new secondary hepatic and bone lesions.

translation:

No vascular abnormalities. According to departmental protocol, we will discuss management in a multidisciplinary team meeting.

INDICATION
AVP moto, traumatisme facial. Probable épistaxis postérieur. Douleurs du bassin. Hyperlactatémie à 4. Fast écho négative.

TECHNIQUE.
Acquisition TDM en contraste spontané sur l'encéphale, puis après injection de produit de contraste au temps artériel sur les troncs supra-aortiques, le thorax et l'abdomen jusqu'aux genoux, portal sur l'abdomen et le pelvis.
Complément effectué par une acquisition tardive à 8 minutes sur l'appareil urinaire.
PDC :
DLP sur l'encéphale: mGy.cm DLP sur le tronc : mGy cm. 

RESULTATS
Au niveau encéphalique :
Petite lame d'hémorragie méningée pariétale bilatérale à hauteur du vertex.
Hémorragie méningée pariéto-occipitale droite avec petites contusions hémorragiques millimétriques associées.
Pas d'œdème cérébral ou d'effet de masse.
Pas d'engagement cérébral ou d'hydrocéphalie.
Pas d'hyperdensité spontanée décelable au sein des vaisseaux intracrâniens.
Pas de plage d'ischémie cortico-sous-corticale récente.
Fracture du rocher droit extralabyrinthique s'étendant à l'os tympanal avec hémotympan et comblement partiel des cellules mastoïdiennes.

-Important fracas du massif facial avec aspect de Lefort 3 bilatéral associant une fracture passant par la racine du nez, une fracture comminutive des os propres du nez déplacée, une fracture de la lame papyracée de manière bilatérale, une fracture passant par les parois latérales des orbites et des arcades zygomatiques, une fracture bilatérale des ptérygoïdes.
-Fracture de toutes les parois du sinus maxillaire gauche avec enfoncement de la paroi latérale et du plancher de l'orbite avec esquille intrasinusale. Trait de fracture comminutif du plancher de l'orbite passant par le canal du V2 gauche. Incarcération graisseuse orbitaire gauche sans incarcération musculaire. 
-Fracture passant par le canal lacrymal gauche.
-Trait de fracture passant niveau de l'apex orbitaire gauche. 
-Fracture de la lame papyracée et de la paroi supérieure du sinus sphénoïdal gauche avec petite bulle de pneumocéphalie à hauteur du canal du nerf optique gauche en faveur d'une brèche ostéoméningée.
-Fracture des parois, interne, latérale et supérieure du sinus maxillaire droit.
-Fracture du plancher de l'orbite droit sans signe d'incarcération. 
-Fracture du toit de l'orbite droit avec probable brèche ostéoméningée sans pneumocéphalie toutefois individualisable en regard.
Important pneumorbite bilatérale.
Pas de fracture formellement individualisable au niveau des canaux des nerfs optiques ou du canal lacrymal droit.
Hémosinus maxillaire bilatérale et sphénoïdale.
-Fracture non déplacée de la branche montante de la mandibule gauche et fracture parasymphysaire gauche de la mandibule passant entre les dents 35 et 36.
Important emphysème sous-cutané périorbitaire et péri mandibulaire droit.

Au niveau du rachis cervical :
Alignement satisfaisant des corps vertébraux.
Pas de lésion osseuse post-traumatique, de luxation, de décoaptation articulaire ou de baillement discal anormal.
Pas d'anomalie des troncs supra-aortiques, en particulier, pas d'argument pour une dissection post-traumatique.

Au niveau thoracique :
Pas d'hémopneumothorax décelable.
Plages en verre dépoli avec épaissement des septa interlobulaires apicales gauches pouvant être en rapport avec une contusion pulmonaire.
Troubles ventilatoires des bases pulmonaires.
Petites lésions d'emphysème paraseptal apicales droites.
Hernie hiatale par glissement.
Intégrité des vaisseaux artériels médiastinaux, en particulier de l'aorte.

A l'étage abdomino-pelvien :
Hémo-sous-péritoine situé sous la vessie au dessus de la symphyse pubienne, de faible à moyenne abondance, sans saignement actif individualisable, sans fracture décelable au niveau du bassin.
Pas de plaie urétérale individualisable sur l'acquisition tardive urinaire. Opacification au temps tardif urinaire incomplète de la vessie ne permettant pas d'exclure formellement une lésion vésicale. Pas de solution de continuité pariétale vésicale toutefois formellement individualisable au temps portal avec présence d'un globe vésical. L'uretère prostatique n'est toutefois pas évaluable sur cet examen.
Absence d'hémopéritoine ou de pneumopéritoine.
Pas de lésion post-traumatique intrahépatique, splénique, surrénaliennes, rénales, pancréatique.
Vésicule biliaire alithiasique.
Absence d'anomalie individualisable au niveau de l'appareil digestif sous réserve d'un examen effectué en l'absence de préparation et d'opacification.
Pas de lésion post traumatique de l'aorte ou des artères à destinée viscérale.

Au niveau osseux :
Fracture articulaire unitubérositaire à la partie antérieure du plateau tibial interne gauche sans enfoncement significatif avec lipohémarthrose associée. Pas d'anomalie vasculaire décelable en regard.
Petite fracture corticale de la tête de la fibula gauche, non déplacée.
Pas de fracture du rachis ou du bassin.
Pas de disjonction de la symphyse pubienne des articulations sacro-iliaques. Pas de fracture du gril costal.

CONCLUSION
-Lame d'hémorragie méningée pariétale bilatérale à hauteur du vertex, pariéto-occipitale droite avec petites contusions hémorragiques millimétriques associées.
-Fracture du rocher droit extralabyrinthique s'étendant à l'os tympanal.
-Important fracas du massif facial (Cf compte-rendu sus-jacent) associant Lefort III bilatéral, une fracture des deux plancher de l'orbite plus importante à gauche avec incarcération graisseuse orbitaire, sans incarcération musculaire, atteinte du canal du nerf V2 gauche, atteinte du canal lacrymal gauche.
-Brèche ostéoméningée avec fracture de la lame papyracée de l'apex orbitaire gauche avec petite bulle de pneumocéphalie en regard, fracture à la partie supérieure de l'orbite droit.
-Fracture de la mandibule bifocale associant une fracture parasymphysaire gauche et une fracture de la branche montante de la mandibule à gauche.
-Contusion pulmonaire apicale gauche.
-Hémo-sous- péritoine sans saignement actif, sans fracture du bassin associée. Pas de plaie urétérale formellement individualisable au temps tardif. L'analyse de la vessie est incomplète compte tenu d'une opacification incomplète au temps tardif urinaire. L'examen ne peut pas écarter non  plus une plaie de l'urètre prostatique. Discuter un complément secondaire par cysto scanner ou cystoscopie après avis urologique.
-Fracture non déplacée articulaire uni tubérositaire du plateau tibial interne gauche avec lipohémarthrose.
-Petite fracture corticale de la tête de la fibula gauche, non déplacée.
translation:
BODY SCAN
March 20, 2021

INDICATION
Motorcycle accident, facial trauma. Suspected posterior epistaxis. Pelvic pain. Elevated lactate level at 4. Negative FAST ultrasound.

TECHNIQUE
CT scan performed without contrast on the brain, followed by contrast-enhanced arterial phase imaging of the supra-aortic trunks, chest, and abdomen down to the knees, and portal phase imaging of the abdomen and pelvis. Additional delayed imaging at 8 minutes for the urinary system.
Contrast Dose:
DLP for the brain: mGy.cm DLP for the trunk: mGy cm.

RESULTS
Brain:
Small bilateral parietal subarachnoid hemorrhage at the vertex.
Right parieto-occipital subarachnoid hemorrhage with small associated hemorrhagic contusions.
No cerebral edema or mass effect.
No brain herniation or hydrocephalus.
No detectable spontaneous hyperdensity within the intracranial vessels.
No recent cortico-subcortical ischemic area.
Fracture of the right petrous bone extending to the tympanic bone with hemotympanum and partial filling of the mastoid cells.

-Significant facial bone fractures with bilateral Le Fort III pattern involving a fracture through the nasal root, displaced comminuted fracture of the nasal bones, bilateral fracture of the lamina papyracea, fractures through the lateral walls of the orbits and zygomatic arches, and bilateral pterygoid fractures.
-Fracture of all walls of the left maxillary sinus with depression of the lateral wall and orbital floor with intrasinus bone fragment. Comminuted fracture of the orbital floor involving the left V2 canal. Left orbital fat entrapment without muscle entrapment.
-Fracture through the left lacrimal canal.
-Fracture at the level of the left orbital apex.
-Fracture of the lamina papyracea and superior wall of the left sphenoid sinus with a small pneumocephalus bubble at the left optic canal indicating a dural breach.
-Fracture of the internal, lateral, and superior walls of the right maxillary sinus.
-Fracture of the right orbital floor without signs of entrapment.
-Fracture of the right orbital roof with probable dural breach, although no pneumocephalus is visible.
Significant bilateral orbital emphysema.
No clearly identifiable fracture of the optic nerve canals or right lacrimal canal.
Bilateral maxillary and sphenoidal hemisinus.
-Non-displaced fracture of the left mandibular ramus and left parasymphyseal fracture passing between teeth 35 and 36.
Significant periorbital and right perimandibular subcutaneous emphysema.

Cervical Spine:
Satisfactory alignment of the vertebral bodies.
No post-traumatic bone lesion, dislocation, joint separation, or abnormal disc widening.
No abnormalities of the supra-aortic trunks, particularly no evidence of post-traumatic dissection.

Thorax:
No detectable hemopneumothorax.
Ground-glass opacities with thickening of the left apical interlobular septa possibly related to pulmonary contusion.
Ventilatory disturbances at the lung bases.
Small right apical paraseptal emphysema lesions.
Sliding hiatal hernia.
Integrity of the mediastinal arterial vessels, particularly the aorta.

Abdominopelvic Region:
Hemoperitoneum located beneath the bladder above the pubic symphysis, of mild to moderate volume, without identifiable active bleeding, no detectable pelvic fracture.
No identifiable ureteral injury on delayed urinary imaging. Incomplete opacification of the bladder on delayed urinary phase, not allowing formal exclusion of a bladder injury. No clearly identifiable bladder wall discontinuity on portal phase with presence of a bladder globe. The prostatic urethra is not assessable in this exam.
No hemoperitoneum or pneumoperitoneum.
No post-traumatic injury to the liver, spleen, adrenal glands, kidneys, or pancreas.
Gallbladder without stones.
No identifiable abnormalities in the digestive system, noting the exam was performed without preparation or opacification.
No post-traumatic injury to the aorta or visceral arteries.

Skeletal:
Non-displaced articular fracture of the anterior part of the left medial tibial plateau with associated lipohemarthrosis. No detectable vascular abnormality in the area.
Small non-displaced cortical fracture of the left fibular head.
No spinal or pelvic fracture.
No disjunction of the pubic symphysis or sacroiliac joints. No rib cage fracture.

CONCLUSION
-Bilateral parietal subarachnoid hemorrhage at the vertex, right parieto-occipital with small associated hemorrhagic contusions.
-Right petrous bone fracture extending to the tympanic bone.
-Significant facial bone fractures (see above report) with bilateral Le Fort III pattern, more significant fracture of both orbital floors on the left with orbital fat entrapment, no muscle entrapment, involvement of the left V2 canal, involvement of the left lacrimal canal.
-Dural breach with fracture of the lamina papyracea at the left orbital apex with a small pneumocephalus bubble, fracture at the superior part of the right orbit.
-Bifocal mandibular fracture with left parasymphyseal fracture and fracture of the left mandibular ramus.
-Left apical pulmonary contusion.
-Hemoperitoneum without active bleeding, no associated pelvic fracture. No formally identifiable ureteral injury on delayed phase. Bladder analysis is incomplete due to incomplete opacification on delayed urinary phase. The exam cannot exclude a prostatic urethral injury. Consider secondary evaluation with cysto-CT or cystoscopy after urological consultation.
-Non-displaced articular fracture of the left medial tibial plateau with lipohemarthrosis.
-Small non-displaced cortical fracture of the left fibular head.

I.R.M. myocardique
 le : 12/07/2024

 
INDICATION :
Suspicion de syndrome de Tako Tsubo.

TECHNIQUE 
Il a été réalisé des séquences petit axe et 4 cavités perfusion, petit axe, grand axe et 4 cavités, rehaussement tardif, petit axe   et 4 cavités Ciné.
DOTAREM 30 ml ,lot 23GD079A01.

RESULTATS
La fraction d'éjection ventriculaire gauche est  normale mesurée à 51%.
Sous réserve d'importants artéfacts au niveau de la base du VG, rendant l'analyse impossible à ce niveau, pas de franche anomalie de la cinétique segmentaire ou globale individualisable sur le reste du VG, en particulier, il n'est pas retrouvé d'akinésie en région antéro-septo-apicale ou septoapicale ce jour.
Épaisseur myocardique semblant conservée.
Pas de dilatation ventriculaire gauche : VTDVG=126 ml =57ml/m², VTSVG=61ml.
Ventricule droit non dilaté, de bonne fonction systolique : FEVD=51% VTDVD=59 ml= 27ml/m², VTSVD= 29ml. 
Après injection de gadolinium, il n'est pas visualisé de trouble perfusionnel.
Sur les séquences de réhaussement tardif, découverte d'une prise de contraste intramyocardique, inféro-latéro-basale sur environ deux segments, d'allure plutôt sous-endocardique non transmurale. L'existence d'un trouble de la cinétique segmentaire à ce niveau n'est pas évaluable compte tenu des artéfacts sur les séquences ciné à ce niveau.
Pas d'autre prise de contraste intramyocardique décelable, en particulier, au niveau antéro-septo-apical ou septoapical.
Par ailleurs, absence de masse intracardiaque anormale décelable.
Pas d'épaississement, d'épanchement ou de prise de contraste péricardique anormale.
Pas d'anomalie extracardiaque.

CONCLUSION
VG normocinétique et normokinétique.
Pas d'anomalie de la cinétique segmentaire ou de prise de contraste anormale retrouvée au niveau antéro-septo-apical ou septoapical.
Découverte d'une prise de contraste intramyocardique d'allure plutôt sous-endocardique inféro-latéro-basale sur environ deux segments, avec analyse de la cinétique segmentaire en regard impossible ce jour en raison d'artéfacts : nécrose myocardique ?
À confronter à l'ensemble du dossier clinicobiologique et d'imagerie à recontrôler en fonction.
translation:
Cardiac MRI  
Date: 07/12/2024

INDICATION:  
Suspected Tako Tsubo syndrome.

TECHNIQUE:  
Short-axis and 4-chamber perfusion sequences were performed, along with short-axis, long-axis, and 4-chamber late enhancement, and short-axis and 4-chamber Cine sequences. DOTAREM 30 ml, lot 23GD079A01.

RESULTS:  
The left ventricular ejection fraction is normal, measured at 51%.  
Due to significant artifacts at the base of the LV, analysis is impossible at this level. No distinct segmental or global wall motion abnormalities are identifiable in the rest of the LV. Specifically, no akinesia is found in the antero-septal-apical or septoapical region today.  
Myocardial thickness appears preserved.  
No left ventricular dilation: LVEDV = 126 ml = 57 ml/m², LVESV = 61 ml.  
The right ventricle is not dilated, with good systolic function: RVEF = 51%, RVEDV = 59 ml = 27 ml/m², RVESV = 29 ml.  
After gadolinium injection, no perfusion defect is visualized.  
On late enhancement sequences, an intramyocardial contrast uptake is discovered in the infero-lateral-basal region over approximately two segments, appearing rather subendocardial and non-transmural. The presence of a segmental wall motion abnormality at this level cannot be assessed due to artifacts on the cine sequences at this level.  
No other intramyocardial contrast uptake is detectable, particularly in the antero-septal-apical or septoapical region.  
Additionally, no abnormal intracardiac mass is detectable.  
No abnormal pericardial thickening, effusion, or contrast uptake.  
No extracardiac abnormalities.

CONCLUSION:  
The LV is normokinetic and normodynamic.  
No segmental wall motion abnormalities or abnormal contrast uptake are found in the antero-septal-apical or septoapical region.  
Discovery of an intramyocardial contrast uptake appearing rather subendocardial in the infero-lateral-basal region over approximately two segments, with segmental wall motion analysis at this level impossible today due to artifacts: myocardial necrosis?  
To be correlated with the overall clinical, biological, and imaging findings for follow-up as needed.

report:
Esame eseguito prima e dopo somministrazione di m.d.c. e.v. (100 ml di iomeron 400) in paziente con sindrome di Budd-Chiari.
Fegato modicamente aumentato di dimensioni in particolare si apprezza ipertrofia del lobo caudato. Il parenchima epatico mostra diffuso enhancement disomogeneo con aspetto a "noce moscata" e le vene sovraepatiche non sono visualizzabili. Presenza di numerosi shunt venosi intraepatici con la formazione di circoli collaterali che drenano nella vena cava superiore. 
Presenza di alcune formazioni epatiche nodulari, marcatamente ipervascolari in fase arteriosa, ed isodense in fase portale e tardiva, la maggiore delle quali in 7 (1 cm), riferibili a noduli tipo iperplasia nodulare focale. 
Pervio il sistema portale e la vena mesenterica superiore.
Regolare aspetto di pancreas, reni, surreni, e milza.
Vescica scarsamente repleta non valutabile.
Presenza di formazione cistica semplice di 3 cm nell'annesso di destra da riferire verosimilmente a follicolo dominante.
Non evidenza di linfoadenomegalie.
Assenza di versamento libero.
CONCLUSIONI : il fegato presenta alterazioni compatibili con Sindromi di Budd-Chiari in fase cronica. Multipli noduli FNH-like. Si suggerisce di effettuare i controlli futuri con RM con mezzo di contrasto epatospecifico.
translation:
CT exam acquired before and after i.v. contrast agent injection (100 ml of Iomeron 400) in patient with Budd Chiari syndrome.
Liver is slightly increased in size, namely with caudate lobe hypertrophy. Liver parenchyma has inhomogeneous enhancement with “nutmeg” appearance and hepatic veins are not visualized. There are innumerable intrahepatic venous shunts with collateral veins draining into superior cava vein. 
Multiple liver nodules, highly hypervascular on arterial phase, and isoattenuating on portal venous and delayed phases, with the largest one being in segment 7 (1 cm), which are suggestive of FNH-like lesions.
Portal vein and superior mesenteric vein are patent.
Normal appearance of pancreas, kidney, adrenals, spleen.
Bladder is almost empty, not assessable.
Cystic lesion of 3 cm in the right adnexa, suggestive for dominant ovarian follicle.
No enlarged lymph nodes.
No free fluid.
CONCLUSION
Liver has changes suggestive of Budd Chiari syndrome in a chronic phase. Multiple FNH-like nodules. We suggest to perform next follow-up with MRI with hepatobiliary contrast agent.

report:
Esame eseguito in urgenza nelle sole condizioni di base in paziente con colica addominale.
In quadro di diverticolosi del colon e del sigma, si rileva in corrispondenza del colon discendente, al terzo distale, si apprezza sfumata iperdensità dell'adipe periviscerale nel cui contesto si apprezzano minute bolle aeree, espressione di perforazione diverticolare. Coesiste discreta quota di aria libera in addome.
Fegato di regolare morfovolumetria a densità ridotta come da steatosi. Multiple puntiformi calcificazioni distrofiche in S2.
Colecisti contratta non valutabile . Vie biliari non dilatate.
Non evidenti alterazioni a carattere d'urgenza di milza, pancreas, surreni e reni (lieve ispessimento dei setti reno-renali e reno-fasciali).
Vescica non repleta, non valutabile.
Prostata aumentata di volume (RX max 5 cm) a densità omogenea.
Non evidenza di versamento libero in addome né significative linfadenopatie addomino-pelviche.
Piccola ernia iatale.
CONCLUSIONI
Diverticolite perforata
translation:
Exam acquired in the urgency setting, without i.v. contrast, in patient with abdominal pain.
In the presence of colonic and sigmoid diverticulosis, there is in the distal third of the descending colon a mild hyperattenuation of the perivisceral fat with some locules of free air, indicating perforated diverticulitis. There is also moderate free air in the abdomen.
Liver has normal morphology and volumetry, with reduced density indicating steatosis. Multiple tiny dystrophic calcifications in segment 2.
Gallbladder is collapsed, not assessable. Biliary tree is not dilated.
There is not any urgent lesion in the spleen, pancreas, adrenals, and kidneys (minimal thickening of the reno-renal and reno-fascial septa).
Bladder is almost empty, not assessable.
Prostate is enlarged (maximum diameter 5 cm), with homogeneous density.
No free fluid or enlarged lymph nodes.
Small hiatal hernia.
CONCLUSION
Perforated diverticulitis

report:
Esame eseguito senza e con mdc ev per "dolore addominale e leucocitosi in paziente con malattia di Crohn". 
Ispessimento parietale concentrico substenosante il lume dell'ultima ansa ileale, con spiccato enhancement mucosale, come da malattia di Crohn in fase attiva, ed associata congestione dei vasa recta afferenti che determinano "aspetto a pettine".
A monte di tale tratto d'ansa substenotico, le anse ileali medio-distali presentano "aspetto impacchettato"  (fistole entero-enteriche complicate da fenomeni aderenziali?) con lume ectasico per un breve tratto (RX max 5 cm) ove si evidenzia livello idro-aereo.
Non ulteriori significativi livelli idro-aerei.
Non versamento né aria  libera in addome.
Alcuni subcentimetrici linfonodi nel contesto del ventaglio mesenteriale. 
Splenomegalia (DL 14 cm) a densità omogenea. 
Non alterazioni a carattere d'urgenza di fegato (lesione focale di 6 mm sfumatamente ipodensa al VII segmento epatico), pancreas, surreni, reni e vescica. 
CONCLUSIONI
Malattia di Crohn in fase attiva.
translation:
Exam acquired before and after i.v. c.a. injection for “abdominal pain and leukocytosis in a patient with Crohn’s disease”.
Substenotic concentric parietal thickening of the last ileal loop, with marked mucosal enhancement, suggestive of Crohn’s disease in the active phase, with associated engorgement of the vasa recta with the “comb sign” appearance. 
The mid-distal ileal loops located upstream to the substenotic one, show a “packed” appearance (entero-enteric fistulae complicated by adhesions?) with enlarged lumen for a small tract (maximum diameter 5 cm) where an air-fluid level is evident.
There are not further significant air-fluid levels.
No free fluid or free air in the abdomen.
Some subcentimetric nodes in the mesentery.
Splenomegaly (CCL 14 cm) with homogeneous density.
There is not any urgent lesion in the liver (focal slightly hypoattenuating lesion of 6 mm  in segment 7), pancreas, adrenals, kidney and bladder.  
CONCLUSIONS
Crohn’s disease in an active phase.
